Comparative evaluation demonstrated higher overall performance than the evaluated baseline architectures, including U-Net, V-Net, ResNet50, and EfficientNet-B7, with statistical differences assessed using paired t-tests at p < 0.05. The results demonstrate that segmentation-guided ROI extraction combined with deep feature-based classification and weighted probabilistic fusion provides an effective approach for automated brain tumor analysis.

title: Refractory Thymoma-Associated Minimal Change Disease Progressing to End-Stage Renal Disease: A Case Report.
abstract: Thymoma-associated minimal change disease (MCD) is an uncommon paraneoplastic cause of nephrotic syndrome in adults. Most reported cases respond to tumor-directed therapy and immunosuppression, but a small subset may be treatment-refractory and progress to renal failure. We report a 52-year-old man with prior resection and adjuvant radiotherapy for Type B2 (Masaoka stage III) thymoma who presented three years after cancer therapy with rapid weight gain, extensive peripheral edema, and frothy urine. Laboratory evaluation revealed nephrotic syndrome with 24-hour proteinuria 12.5 g, serum albumin 1.8 g/dL, and creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. Renal biopsy showed normal glomeruli on light microscopy, negative immunofluorescence, and diffuse podocyte foot-process effacement on electron microscopy, consistent with MCD. Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day failed to produce remission after four weeks. Staging with CT-PET identified an anterior mediastinal node consistent with recurrent thymoma, which was treated with targeted radiotherapy. Despite sequential immunomodulatory therapies-oral cyclophosphamide (months 2-8), tacrolimus (months 8-14), and two doses of rituximab (months 14-15)-proteinuria fluctuated but persisted at nephrotic levels and renal function progressively declined, with creatinine rising to 7.0 mg/dL by month 18, necessitating initiation of renal replacement therapy. The patient developed uremic symptoms and by month 18 required initiation of hemodialysis, ultimately transitioning to chronic peritoneal dialysis. This case documents an unusually aggressive course of thymoma-associated MCD refractory to multiple lines of immunosuppression and tumor-directed therapy, culminating in end-stage renal disease. It underscores that, although thymoma-related MCD is often steroid-responsive, clinicians should recognize the potential for refractory disease and consider early multidisciplinary management, vigilant oncologic surveillance, and exploration of alternative or targeted immunologic strategies in such patients.

title: Autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation affects paramagnetic rim lesions in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Background Available literature shows a marginal or no effect of disease-modifying therapies on paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs), a promising magnetic resonance imaging marker of chronic inflammation in multiple sclerosis. Objective To investigate longitudinal changes in PRL count in people with multiple sclerosis treated with autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHSCT), exploring their potential as predictors of treatment response. Methods Monocentric study including 30 AHSCT-treated people with multiple sclerosis who performed at least two brain magnetic resonance imaging scans with susceptibility-weighted imaging either (i) before and after AHSCT (pre/post-AHSCT group; n = 12) or (ii) after AHSCT only (post-AHSCT group; n = 18). Results In the pre/post-AHSCT group, PRL count decreased in 2/5 (40%) PRL-positive cases over a median of 21 (7-74) months; 5/26 (19%) PRL s resolved. In the post-AHSCT group, PRL count decreased in 4/7 (57%) PRL -positive cases over a median of 51 (6-57) months; 10/20 (50%) PRL s resolved. The annualised paramagnetic rim lesion disappearance rate was -0.36 and -0.43 in the two groups, respectively. No new PRL appeared. Baseline PRL count correlated with disability in the pre/post-AHSCT group only (r = 0.741, p = 0.006). Conclusions Given the reported long persistence of PRLs, these data indicate that AHSCT may accelerate their disappearance, suggesting an effect within the central nervous system on microglia/macrophages. PRLs could predict response to central nervous system-bioavailable treatments.

title: Survivor bias and disease progression in observational cohorts in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Background Long-term studies on multiple sclerosis progression often face dropout, possibly among those with more aggressive disease, biasing the cohort. Objectives We assessed potential survivorship bias in a long-term observational multiple sclerosis cohort. Methods Three hundred sixty-one patients with multiple sclerosis were followed for 10 years, with clinical assessments, blood biomarkers and magnetic resonance imaging at baseline, follow-up 1 and follow-up 2. Progression was defined as an Expanded Disability Status Scale increase. Dropout was analysed and predicted; estimated Expanded Disability Status Scale was calculated for dropouts to assess bias. Brain volumes were normalized. Results One hundred and sixty-two patients with multiple sclerosis completed all follow-ups; 81 showed progression. Dropout rates were 97/361 at follow-up 1 and 102/264 at follow-up 2. Dropouts had worse Expanded Disability Status Scale, Nine-Hole Peg test, Timed 25-Foot Walk, lower brain volume and higher lesion volume before dropping out. Blood biomarkers did not differ. Main dropout predictors were higher baseline Expanded Disability Status Scale, lesion volume, worse Nine-Hole Peg test and shorter disease duration. Median estimated Expanded Disability Status Scale at follow-up 2 for dropouts was 5.5 versus 3.5 for non-dropouts. Discussion Fewer than half completed the study. High lesion load and worse clinical status predicted dropout. This may cause underestimation of progression and reduced statistical power. Similar bias may affect other long-term studies in chronic diseases.

title: Pedal acceleration time-Guided management of diabetic foot ulcers with borderline ischemia.
abstract: Background: The management of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) with borderline ischemia remains challenging due to the absence of reliable physiological markers to guide revascularization decisions. Pedal acceleration time (PAT) is a Doppler-derived measure of distal perfusion that may improve risk stratification. This study aimed to evaluate a PAT-guided management strategy in patients with DFUs and borderline perfusion by assessing its ability to guide treatment allocation, and its association with wound healing and amputation-free survival (AFS). Methods: In this prospective quasi-experimental study, 263 consecutive patients with DFUs and abnormal ankle-brachial index (ABI) findings were enrolled. PAT was measured using duplex ultrasound of the pedal arteries. A predefined cutoff of ⩾ 180 ms was used to guide treatment allocation: patients with a PAT ⩾ 180 ms underwent endovascular revascularization, whereas those with a PAT < 180 ms underwent debridement alone. Primary outcomes included AFS, wound healing, major adverse limb events (MALE), and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at 24 months. The diagnostic accuracy of PAT for detecting significant infrapopliteal stenosis was assessed using conventional angiography as the reference standard. Results: At 24 months, AFS was higher in the revascularization group than in the debridement-alone group, although this difference was not statistically significant (64.2% vs 58.4%; p = 0.344). However, a Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a significant difference in AFS over the follow-up period (log-rank p < 0.05). Overall survival and freedom from reintervention did not differ significantly between groups. Multivariable analysis identified advanced stages of the Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and a higher PAT category as predictors of major amputation. Advanced WIfI stage was also associated with nonhealing, and the PAT category showed a borderline association with nonhealing. A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance of PAT for detecting significant arterial stenosis, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88. At a cutoff ⩾ 180 ms, sensitivity was 84.0% (95% CI 76.6-89.4) and specificity was 81.2% (95% CI 73.8-86.8), with an overall accuracy of 82.5%. Conclusions: PAT provides a useful physiological adjunct to distal perfusion assessment in DFUs with borderline ischemia. A threshold of ⩾ 180 ms identifies patients with hemodynamically significant disease, and it is associated with improved risk stratification for revascularization. These findings support further evaluation of PAT as an adjunctive assessment tool in patients with borderline ischemia.

title: Emerging hydrogel platforms for disease modeling, diagnosis, and imaging of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the presence of amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, neurodegeneration, cognitive decline, and dementia. The exact pathogenesis is not well understood, as appropriate pathological and therapeutically relevant disease models remain limited. Hydrogels are hydrophilic, three-dimensional (3D) polymer networks composed of synthetic or natural materials and have diverse neuroscience applications, including drug delivery, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine. Currently, hydrogel in vitro platforms are becoming increasingly explored for AD pathogenesis, as brain extracellular matrix-mimicking biodegradable components, for delivery of growth factors for neurons and other brain cells, AD-specific peptide release, engineered multi-region brain organoids, and therapeutic drug delivery. Beyond disease modeling, hydrogels are being used to evaluate emerging AD diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, such as biomarker sensing and the integration of imaging. Recent AD diagnostic platforms have leveraged hydrogels as biomolecule-capture matrices and signal-transduction elements to detect AD-associated biomarkers via minimally invasive or implantable systems. Hydrogels have also been harnessed in magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, computed tomography, and positron emission tomography imaging modalities to support imageable vehicles for therapeutic delivery. Such platforms hold promise for bridging physiologically relevant neurobiological investigation with more accessible, efficient clinical tools for AD. This review highlights recent advances in hydrogel-based disease models, diagnostic tools, and imaging technologies and their potential to integrate with brain organoids, artificial intelligence, and 3D printing to enhance mechanistic and translational applications for AD.

title: An exploratory synthetic MRI-derived FLAIR-DIR contrast in olfactory-limbic regions in mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: BackgroundOdor identification impairment is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease and predicts memory decline, but its microstructural basis remains unclear.ObjectiveTo evaluate FD, a semi-quantitative synthetic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived Fluid-Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR)-Double Inversion Recovery (DIR) contrast, against myelin volume fraction (MVF) in olfactory-limbic brain regions of patients diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).MethodsSixteen healthy controls (HC) and 17 individuals diagnosed with MCI completed olfactory and cognitive testing and underwent 3T MRI using a QALAS sequence. MVF maps were generated and FD was computed as (FLAIR - DIR)/FLAIR. Group differences were examined in olfactory-limbic gray matter and associated white-matter tracts, and voxel-wise regression assessed FD-odor identification associations, including models adjusted for voxel-wise MVF. Region of interest and voxel-wise analyses were exploratory and largely uncorrected for multiple comparisons.ResultsCompared with HC, MCI showed lower FD across olfactory-limbic gray matter and white-matter pathways, including hippocampus, amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex, thalamus and corpus callosum, whereas MVF differences were more limited. Better odor identification was associated with higher FD in hippocampal/parahippocampal regions and insula, persisting after MVF adjustment. MVF showed positive associations in the right parahippocampal gyrus, left thalamus and genu of the corpus callosum. In an exploratory secondary analysis reported in the Supplemental Material, FD-based classification exceeded chance but was not separable from age alone.ConclusionsFD is a semi-quantitative relaxation-contrast metric showing regional patterns partially distinct from MVF. These exploratory findings require replication in larger, demographically matched, biomarker-confirmed cohorts before FD can be regarded as a marker of early olfactory-limbic microstructural change in MCI.

title: Changes in gray matter volume associated with gait speed and muscle mass in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: BackgroundMild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an early stage of cognitive decline between normal aging and dementia. Gait speed, a key marker of physical function, has been associated with both cognitive decline and brain atrophy. Sarcopenia, characterized by age-related loss of muscle mass and function, has also been linked to structural brain changes.ObjectiveTo investigate the associations between sarcopenia, its individual components and regional gray matter volume (GMV) in older adults with MCI.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 234 older adults with MCI. Sarcopenia, gait speed, handgrip strength, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI) were assessed according to the 2019 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. Brain T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging was analyzed using voxel-based morphometry. Voxel-wise group comparisons were performed to identify GMV differences after adjustment age, sex, comorbidity, depressive symptoms, nutritional status, and total intracranial volume.ResultsSlower gait speed was significantly associated with lower GMV in the bilateral putamen and left superior frontal cortex. Lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV in the left inferior temporal cortex. No significant GMV differences were found by sarcopenia status or handgrip strength.ConclusionsSlower gait speed is associated with reduced GMV in motor-related brain regions, indicating early brain structural changes in older adults with MCI. Although lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV, this finding should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight the complex interactions between physical function and brain structure, emphasizing gait speed as a potential indicator of brain health in older adults with MCI.

title: Circulating Metalloproteinase Inhibitors and Artificial Intelligence-Derived Radiomics Predict Persistent Endoleak After Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Multimodal Biological-Imaging Model.
abstract: Objective Persistent endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) reflects ongoing aneurysm sac biological activity and remains insufficiently predicted by anatomical surveillance alone. We aimed to evaluate whether integration of circulating matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), and artificial intelligence (AI)-derived radiomic features from computed tomographic angiography (CTA) improves prediction of persistent endoleak. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study including 62 consecutive patients undergoing elective infrarenal EVAR between January 2020 and December 2024. Plasma levels of MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-9, MMP-10, TIMP-1, and TIMP-2 were measured preoperatively and at 1 and 12 months post-EVAR. Computed tomography angiography data sets were analyzed using a standardized semi-automated radiomics pipeline with reproducibility testing and penalized feature selection. The primary endpoint was persistent endoleak at 12 months. Multivariable logistic regression was constructed with event-per-variable control and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Results Persistent endoleak occurred in 18 patients (29%). Patients with persistent endoleak exhibited significantly higher MMP-9 levels, lower TIMP-1 and TIMP-2 levels, and markedly elevated MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratios at 1 month (all P < .01). Radiomics demonstrated increased intraluminal thrombus (ILT) entropy and reduced ILT density in the endoleak group. A parsimonious model including MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio and ILT entropy yielded an optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) of 0.81 with good calibration, outperforming sac diameter change alone (AUC = 0.62). Conclusions Persistent endoleak is associated with systemic proteolytic imbalance and imaging-detectable thrombus heterogeneity. Integration of biological and radiomic markers improves risk stratification compared with morphological surveillance alone and warrants prospective validation.Clinical ImpactThis study proposes a novel multimodal approach to post-EVAR surveillance by integrating circulating metalloproteinase inhibitors with AI-derived CT radiomics. Combining biological biomarkers with quantitative analysis of peri-EVAR thrombus volume and density may improve identification of patients at risk of persistent endoleak beyond conventional imaging assessment. For clinicians, this approach could enable earlier risk stratification, support personalised surveillance intervals, and identify patients who may benefit from closer imaging follow-up or intervention. The innovation lies in integrating systemic biological activity with local imaging phenotypes within a predictive model, moving EVAR surveillance from a predominantly anatomical strategy towards a personalised, data-driven biological-imaging paradigm.

title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
abstract: ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R 2 = 0.72; P < 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. title: A Study on Renal Artery Variations by CT Angiography and Their Clinical Importance.
abstract: AimThis study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, anatomical variations, and branching patterns of the renal arteries using multiphasic computed tomography angiography (CTA), based on the modified classification proposed by Cases et al (2017). Understanding renal artery variations is essential for preoperative planning, renal transplantation, endovascular procedures, and urological interventions.Materials and MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 1220 abdominal CTA studies performed between March 2020 and June 2024. Fourteen cases were excluded according to predetermined exclusion criteria, resulting in 1206 studies being included in the final analysis (700 males, 520 females). All examinations were performed using a 128-slice CT scanner (Siemens SOMATOM; syngo CT VC 40). CTA protocols included 5-mm acquisition and 1-mm reconstruction, with administration of 100-120 mL of iodinated contrast at 5-6 mL/s via an 18G antecubital cannula. Post-processing involved multiplanar reformation, volume rendering, and 3D reconstruction. Two experienced radiologists independently reviewed all studies. Renal arteries were categorized into Types A-E and Patterns I-V. "Early division" (Types B and E) and "polar branches" (Types C and D) were further grouped for analytical purposes.ResultsAmong 1206 CTA studies, Type A (normal hilar artery) was the most common in both kidneys, with a slightly higher prevalence on the right (74.29%) than on the left (67.99%). Polar branches were more frequent in the left kidney, whereas early divisions were more common in the right kidney. Pattern 1 was predominant bilaterally (RK: 85.73%; LK: 77.61%), followed by Pattern 2. Significant differences were observed between the kidneys in the distribution of Types A, C, D, and Patterns 1 and 2.ConclusionCTA provides excellent visualization of renal artery variations, enabling precise classification and improving surgical, interventional, and transplant planning. Recognition of these anatomical differences is essential for minimizing procedural complications.

title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

title: Knee Arthroscopy for Wear-Induced Synovitis of a Recalled Implant Is Associated With a High Rate of Failure and Fails to Avoid Need for Revision TKA.
abstract: Background Polyethylene wear-induced synovitis and osteolysis are well-recognized complications following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and have been of particular concern in the setting of recalled Exactech implants. While knee arthroscopy (KA) has been proposed as a minimally invasive option to address intra-articular debris and synovitis, its effectiveness in preventing disease progression and implant failure remains unclear. Purposes The purpose of this study was to evaluate the clinical and radiographic outcomes of KA in patients with recalled Exactech TKA presenting with polyethylene wear-induced synovitis. Specifically, we assessed rates of reoperation, revision arthroplasty, and progression of osteolysis following arthroscopic intervention. Methods A retrospective chart review was conducted on 38 patients who underwent KA after primary TKA with recalled Exactech implants between January 2022 and January 2023. Patient demographics, clinical outcomes, and radiographic and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings were analyzed by a high-volume, fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon. Results Within 1 year of follow-up, 4/38 patients (10.5%) underwent revision TKA, 4/38 (10.5%) patients underwent repeat KA, and 6/38 patients (15.8%) demonstrated progressive osteolysis on follow-up radiographs, resulting in an overall failure rate of 14/38 patients (36.8%). Of the remaining 30 patients who had not undergone revision TKA or repeat KA, 29 of 30 patients (96.7%) had one of the following findings: possible component loosening (5/30), progressive radiolucent lines (25/30), and worsening osteolysis on follow-up radiographs (15/30). Additionally, upon review of patient post-arthroscopy MRIs, 28/30 patients (93.3%) had documentation of persistent/progressive polymeric-induced synovitis or persistent/progressive osteolysis. Conclusion The high failure rate reported in the current study suggests that KA with debridement is not an appropriate treatment for patients with polyethylene wear-induced synovitis and osteolysis following the implantation of a recalled Exactech TKA. Delay of the surgery can result in more severe bone defects. In patients with wear-induced synovitis but without osteolysis or implant loosening, a polyethylene insert exchange is the preferred alternative treatment. Level of evidence Prognostic study level IV.

title: Why clinicians in acute hospitals may fail to engage in direct communication with people with intellectual disability.
abstract: This case highlights the healthcare inequities faced by people with intellectual disability, including diagnostic overshadowing, communication barriers, and the need for personalised, meaningful adjustments in care. A woman in her fifties with mild intellectual disability, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus experienced delayed diagnosis and treatment because healthcare providers assumed she could not tolerate magnetic resonance imaging; however, when the scan was eventually completed with supported communication, it revealed a serious brain tumour with metastases. The case shows that diagnostic overshadowing can arise not only from misattributing symptoms, but also from untested assumptions about a patient's ability to engage with diagnostic procedures. It also underscores the importance of involving patients and families directly in healthcare decisions to support autonomy and prevent avoidable harm. Addressing these systemic issues is essential to deliver equitable, patient-centred care in acute hospital settings.

title: A quantitative trigger model to enable personalized adaptive radiotherapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
abstract: Background Adaptive radiotherapy (ART) is increasingly used for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), yet optimal triggers remain undefined. Objectives This study developed a quantitative trigger model integrating clinical expertise with morphological and dosimetric changes during treatment to support personalized, scalable ART decision-making. Design This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study conducted at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. Methods Between 2022 and 2024, 60 NPC patients treated on an integrated ART platform (uRT-linac 506c) were enrolled. Forty patients who underwent ART at least once during radiotherapy constituted the training set; morphological and dosimetric parameters between the original treatment plan and fractional radiotherapy were quantified, weighted, and modeled using clinician-simulated ART timing as the reference. The remaining 20 patients (17 with ART and 3 without) served as the validation set. Results A total of 1,466 fan-beam CT scans from 60 patients (40 training, 20 validation) were analyzed. A weighted Trigger Score (TS) was developed, combining volumetric and dosimetric scores in target volumes and key organs-at-risk (parotids, submandibular glands, thyroid, brainstem, spinal cord, optic nerves, chiasm, and temporal lobes). Two trigger modes were defined: 1) an absolute TS ≥65 points, or 2) a TS change ratio ≥1.5 (=TS_y × (y - 2)/Σ TS_2: TS_(y-1), where y = fraction number). In the validation cohort, the model showed high concordance with clinician-simulated triggers, achieving ROC-AUCs of 0.879 (daily) and 0.872 (weekly). The model has been integrated into our clinical ART platform for operational use. Conclusion We developed and validated a transparent, quantitative trigger model integrating clinical expertise with quantified volumetric/dosimetric changes and structural prioritization to enable individualized ART decision-making for NPC. This model supports automated, real-time ART triggering with adjustable thresholds, adaptable to imaging frequencies, and customizable to institutional practice. However, multicenter or prospective validation is still warranted before widespread clinical adoption.

title: Diffuse Serous Atrophy of Bone Marrow in the Ankle and Hindfoot with Focal Acute Lateral Malleolar Osteomyelitis: A Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Based Case Report.
abstract: Serous atrophy of bone marrow (SABM) is a rare marrow disorder associated with severe chronic illness and malnutrition. It results in characteristic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signal due to atrophy of fat cells and loss of hematopoietic cells with deposition of gelatinous material. This may be misinterpreted as a technical error from the MRI scanner or mimic infiltrative or infectious processes. We report a case of a 71-year-old severely malnourished and immunosuppressed man with a full-thickness ulcer over the right lateral malleolus who underwent an MRI of the right ankle without and with intravenous gadolinium contrast for evaluation of suspected osteomyelitis. Pre-contrast MRI images demonstrated diffuse abnormal marrow signal throughout the ankle and hindfoot consistent with SABM, given his profound cachexia and malnutrition. Post-contrast images demonstrated a small focus of enhancement at the lateral malleolus beneath the patient's ulcer, suggesting an additional diagnosis of acute osteomyelitis without cortical destruction. The marrow signal in SABM and osteomyelitis can be indistinguishable on non-contrast MRI sequences; post-contrast imaging and correlation with clinical examination are essential, as SABM does not demonstrate contrast enhancement and acute osteomyelitis demonstrates enhancement. Given the patient's frailty and poor healing capacity, conservative management was pursued. Recognizing SABM and osteomyelitis in the ankle and foot requires integration of the clinical context with MRI findings, in which invasive procedures and misdiagnosis can be avoided.

title: Efficacy of Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Sampling in Muscle Tears and Intersex Differences in Professional Football Players: A Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the gold standard for monitoring the evolution of muscle injuries in athletes, although no established quantitative measure of recovery currently exists. Hypothesis Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values may provide a quantitative measure of muscle healing, and sex-related differences may exist in the evolution of muscle injuries. Study design Single-center retrospective observational cohort study. Level of evidence Level 2a. Methods Twenty-six professional football (soccer) players (13 male ,13 female) undergoing MRI for muscle injury were retrospectively selected between October 2020 and June 2024. All athletes underwent MRI at baseline (T0) and at 2-week follow-up, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) acquisitions with b values of 0-100-800 s/mm ² . Two musculoskeletal radiologists measured ADC values within the index lesions at each examination. Changes in ADC between the two time points (ΔADC) were assessed using a paired-samples t test, while sex-related differences were evaluated using the Mann-Whitney U test. Results The overall mean ADC value at the lesion site decreased from 2.06 ± 0.35 mm 2 /s at T0 to 1.61 ± 0.30 mm 2 /s at follow-up corresponding to a mean ΔADC of 0.44 ± 0.20 and a 21.84% reduction. The difference between T0 and follow-up was statistically significant ( t = 8.12; P < 0.001). Mean ΔADC values were 0.32 ± 0.20 mm ² /s in male players and 0.56 ± 0.25 mm ² /s in female players, respectively, with a statistically significant difference between sexes (z = -2.95; P = 0.003). When only hamstring injuries were considered, female players showed a significantly greater decrease in ADC over time than male players (Mann-Whitney U test; exact P = 0.02), with mean ΔADC values of 0.56 ± 0.30 and 0.26 ± 0.08 mm ² /s, respectively. Conclusion Muscle injury is associated with an acute increase in ADC values followed by a progressive decrease during healing. ADC may therefore represent a quantitative imaging biomarker for monitoring muscle recovery. Clinical relevance ADC measurement within muscle tears may provide a quantitative assessment of healing status and support individualized rehabilitation strategies in athletes. Sex-related differences may exist in injury pathophysiology and recovery patterns relevant to safe return to play.

title: Alexander Disease Diagnosed in an Obstetrics Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare autosomal dominant leukodystrophy due to pathogenic variants in glial fibrillary acidic protein ( GFAP) . Adult-onset AxD type II presents with heterogeneous neurologic and neuropsychiatric symptoms. We report a unique case diagnosed in the postpartum period that mimicked posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). A 33-year-old gravida 2 para 1 at 36 weeks gestation presented with 10 days of progressive restlessness, delusions, insomnia, dysarthria, weight loss with inability to feed herself, and urinary/fecal incontinence. She underwent induction of labor due to concern for severe pre-eclampsia (elevated liver enzymes and creatine kinase, elevated blood pressure), received magnesium sulfate, and required emergent cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal status. However, her symptoms persisted postpartum. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed extensive bifrontal, periventricular, and pontine non-enhancing hyperintensities. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was normal including negative infectious, autoimmune, and paraneoplastic studies. Electroencephalography showed mild background slowing but no epileptiform activity. Empiric methylprednisolone and acyclovir had limited effects. Given the imaging findings, a leukodystrophy panel was ordered, which identified a heterozygous pathogenic GFAP variant (Arg79Leu), confirming a diagnosis of AxD type II. She improved with rehabilitation, with mild residual dysarthria at the 2-month follow-up. This is the first case report to describe an onset of AxD in the peripartum period. In peripartum patients with neurological symptoms whose course and MRI findings are atypical for PRES or other more common disorders, adult-onset neurogenetic disorders such as AxD should be considered. This diagnosis has important reproductive implications and warrants genetic counseling.

title: Baseline Knee Extension Is Associated With Volumetric Femoral Cartilage Loss in the Central Region of the Mid-lateral and External Medial Femoral Condyles: Data From the Osteoarthritis Initiative.
abstract: ObjectiveData evaluating knee flexion contracture (FC)-associated regional changes on femoral articular cartilage are lacking. We compared regional femoral articular cartilage outcomes of people with knee osteoarthritis (OA) with and without FC using quantitative MRI data.MethodsArticular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyles were segmented into internal, central, and external subregions on MRI. Goniometry measured knee extension. We tested for regional differences in cartilage thickness and percent denuded bone (i.e., 0mm cartilage thickness) in the presence or absence of FC, and for associations between cartilage outcomes with quantitative knee extension range of motion (ROM) using a linear model for 596 participants.ResultsFor FC versus no FC, cartilage thickness in the central lateral subregion was higher (2.36±0.42mm vs. 2.29±0.43mm; p<0.05), with higher percent denuded bone in the central lateral (0.92±3.5% vs. 0.39±2.2%; p<0.05) and central medial subregions (4.61±12.88% vs. 3.17±11.66%; p<0.05). Lost knee extension was associated with increased percent denuded bone in the internal lateral ( r= 0.095; p<0.05), central lateral ( r =0.90; p<0.05), and central medial subregions ( r =0.117 ; p<0.01) but with increased central lateral cartilage thickness ( r =0.110; p<0.01). After correcting for clinical factors, an association between lost knee extension and increased percent denuded bone remained in the central lateral femur [ β =0.059; (95% CI 0.003-0.114)].ConclusionConclusion: Lost knee extension was associated with increased percent denuded bone in the central lateral and external medial femur. Interventions to maintain and/or restore knee ROM may benefit femoral cartilage health. Longitudinal studies evaluating the impact of lost knee ROM on femoral cartilage are warranted.

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics model for preoperative prediction of IDH1 R132H immunopositivity status in adult diffuse Glioma.
abstract: Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors, and isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status is a critical molecular marker influencing prognosis and treatment planning. This study aimed to evaluate the value of a multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics model in predicting IDH1 R132H immunopositivity status in patients with gliomas. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 94 adult glioma patients at Viet Duc University Hospital from June 2024 to January 2026. All patients underwent preoperative MRI including conventional sequences, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion imaging (DSC-MRI). Radiomics features were extracted from apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) and relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV) maps within the tumor region, followed by correlation filtering and LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator)-based feature selection, retaining 5 ADC and 10 rCBV features for logistic regression model construction. The ADC-based model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.875, the rCBV-based model reached 0.943, and the combined model achieved the highest numerical AUC (0.955), with an accuracy of 89.5%, sensitivity of 87.5%, and specificity of 90.9%, although the differences between models were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that multiparametric MRI radiomics demonstrates promising discriminatory performance for preoperative prediction of IDH1 R132H immunopositivity status in glioma patients, although these estimates derive from a single-center cohort with a small held-out test set and therefore require external validation in larger, prospective cohorts.

title: Combined qualitative and quantitative MRI reveals short-term progression in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.
abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is characterized by slowly progressive and heterogeneous muscle involvement; therefore, clinical measures show limited sensitivity to short-term change. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides useful biomarkers of muscle degeneration and disease activity. To investigate one-year longitudinal changes in lower leg muscles of patients with FSHD using qualitative (T1-weighted [T1w], STIR) and quantitative MRI (fat fraction [FF], water T2), and to assess their relationship with clinical function. Thirty-one patients with FSHD (21 men; age 44.2±17 years) and 30 matched controls underwent 3T MRI. Twenty-seven patients completed one-year follow-up. Semi-quantitative grading and quantitative measures were analyzed muscle-wise. Longitudinal changes and correlations with clinical scores were assessed. At baseline, T1w imaging showed marked inter- and intra-individual variability, with heterogeneous proximal-distal involvement in 22% of muscles and asymmetric involvement in 77% of patients. STIR hyperintensity was present in 25 patients. Over one-year, clinical decline was small (MRC: Δ=-0.26, p=0.018, SRM=-0.23; mobility: Δ=-0.41, p=0.031, SRM=-0.44). In contrast, quantitative MRI detected progression, with increases in FF (0.17±0.13 to 0.22±0.15, p<0.001, SRM=0.87), FF heterogeneity, and water T2 heterogeneity, while T1w scores and mean water T2 showed limited change. Progression was greatest in muscles with intermediate baseline FF (ΔFF/year: 0.049 vs 0.007, p<0.001). Baseline STIR and water T2 abnormalities predicted increases in FF but not T1w scores. FF correlated more strongly with clinical measures than T1w grading. Quantitative MRI is more sensitive than qualitative grading for detecting short-term disease progression in FSHD. Measures of heterogeneity and disease activity predict structural progression and represent promising biomarkers for clinical trials.

title: Preoperative MRI-Derived Deltoid Morphometry and Early Pain and Functional Recovery After Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: A Size-Normalized, Segment-Specific Analysis.
abstract: Background The deltoid is a primary compensatory motor for shoulder elevation and may influence early recovery after rotator cuff repair. Hypothesis/purpose The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived deltoid morphometry, normalized to humeral head diameter, is associated with early postoperative function and pain after arthroscopic repair of full-thickness supraspinatus tears (± infraspinatus involvement). We hypothesized that greater size-normalized deltoid thickness-particularly posterior thickness-would be associated with superior early functional outcomes and lower pain. Study design Cohort study; Level of evidence, 3. Methods A retrospective cohort of 38 patients who underwent primary arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR) for full-thickness supraspinatus tears (± infraspinatus) was analyzed. Preoperative MRI was used to quantify anterior, middle, and posterior deltoid thickness, deltoid cross-sectional area (CSA), and humeral head diameter. Size-normalized indices were calculated as thickness/diameter for each deltoid segment and as (CSA/diameter 2 ). Clinical outcomes included Constant score and visual analog scale (VAS) pain assessed preoperatively and at the standardized routine 3-month postoperative follow-up; change scores were calculated as ΔConstant and ΔVAS. Results The mean age was 56.7 ± 6.4 years, and 60.5% of patients were women. Clinical outcomes improved significantly at the routine 3-month postoperative follow-up, with the Constant score increasing from 38.8 ± 6.7 to 51.6 ± 8.5 and the VAS pain score decreasing from 6.7 ± 1 to 3.4 ± 1.1 (both P < .001). After false discovery rate correction, posterior deltoid thickness index showed the strongest associations with early outcomes. Posterior deltoid thickness index was associated with higher 3-month postoperative Constant score ( r = 0.686 [95% CI, 0.469 to 0.825]; P < .001; Q < 0.001) and lower 3-month postoperative VAS pain ( r = -0.600 [95% CI, -0.771 to -0.346]; P < .001; Q = 0.001). In exploratory adjusted regression, posterior deltoid thickness index remained associated with 3-month postoperative Constant score and VAS pain after adjustment for age, sex, and tear size. Conclusion Preoperative size-normalized, segment-specific deltoid morphometry on MRI, particularly posterior deltoid thickness, may be associated with early pain and functional recovery after ARCR. These exploratory findings require prospective validation before clinical use.

title: The Influence of Screw Height Placement on Syndesmotic Malreduction: A Cadaveric Study.
abstract: Background Syndesmotic malreduction is a well-documented complication impacting ankle fracture outcomes. Although syndesmotic screw fixation remains the most common method for stabilization, optimal screw height placement has not been rigorously evaluated in terms of its impact on reduction accuracy. This cadaveric study aimed to assess the influence of screw height placement on syndesmotic alignment in a simulated pronation-external rotation (PER) ankle fracture model. Methods Ten knee disarticulated cadaveric specimens underwent simulated PER injuries. Quad-cortical syndesmotic screws were incrementally placed at different levels at 0.6-cm intervals, ranging from 1.5 to 6.3 cm above the plafond. At each level, the syndesmosis was manually open reduced, stabilized, and imaged using computed tomography. Syndesmotic alignment was assessed using standard axial 2-D measurements and 3-D volumetric analysis. For each screw height placement, radiographic parameters were compared to the intact state. Results Screw height placement significantly influenced syndesmotic alignment across all measured parameters. Fibular rotation and translation both varied significantly with screw level ( P < .01), as did anterior, mid, and posterior diastasis (all P < .01). Three-dimensional volumetric analysis also showed a significant difference between screw levels ( P < .01). A screw placed 2.7 cm above the tibial plafond resulted in alignment measurements closest to native across 2-D and 3-D measurements. With the numbers available, no correlation could be detected between surgeon variability, incisural morphology, and malreduction. Conclusion This study suggests that screw height placement can influence the quality of syndesmotic reduction in a simulated PER ankle fracture model. A screw placed 2.7 cm above the tibial plafond most closely approximated native syndesmotic alignment and may minimize the risk of malreduction. Clinical relevance Given the reported incidence of syndesmotic malreduction and its association with worse outcomes, understanding whether screw height placement is a modifiable risk factor may inform intraoperative technique during syndesmotic fixation.

title: Evaluation of Management Pathways for Pseudophakic Cystoid Macular Edema in a Large United States Cohort.
abstract: Purpose To identify the common management pathways in the treatment of pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (CME). Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2005 to 2024 using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with pseudophakic CME were included in the study, and patients with retinal comorbidities were excluded. Treatments initiated after the diagnosis of pseudophakic CME, including topical corticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), periocular and intravitreal (IVT) corticosteroids, antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections, suprachoroidal corticosteroids, and pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), were tracked, and treatment sequences and imaging use over time were analyzed. Results A total of 23 035 patients met the inclusion criteria, with a mean age of 72 years; 54% were women, and 68% identified as White. The incidence of pseudophakic CME increased from 2.45% in 2005 to 17.6% in 2024. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) use increased over time, becoming the most common imaging modality (used in 90% of cases), while 20% of patients underwent no imaging. No treatment was documented in 40% of patients. Among those treated, 77% received topical corticosteroids and/ or NSAIDs as first-line therapy, followed by IVT steroids (7.4%), periocular steroids (6.5%), PPV (3.4%), and anti-VEGF injections (2%). IVT steroids were the most common second-line treatment (10.2%), primarily dexamethasone implants (82.8%), followed by triamcinolone (12.2%). Use of newer agents, including fluocinolone acetonide implants and suprachoroidal triamcinolone, was uncommon. Conclusions Despite the increased use of OCT and earlier detection of subclinical cases, a substantial proportion of patients with pseudophakic CME have no documented treatment. Topical steroids and/ or NSAIDs represent the most common first- line therapy, with IVT steroids commonly used after inadequate response to treatment.

Among those treated, 77% received topical corticosteroids and/ or NSAIDs as first-line therapy, followed by IVT steroids (7.4%), periocular steroids (6.5%), PPV (3.4%), and anti-VEGF injections (2%). IVT steroids were the most common second-line treatment (10.2%), primarily dexamethasone implants (82.8%), followed by triamcinolone (12.2%). Use of newer agents, including fluocinolone acetonide implants and suprachoroidal triamcinolone, was uncommon.

Conclusions

Despite the increased use of OCT and earlier detection of subclinical cases, a substantial proportion of patients with pseudophakic CME have no documented treatment. Topical steroids and/ or NSAIDs represent the most common first- line therapy, with IVT steroids commonly used after inadequate response to treatment.

title: Germ line landscape stratification defines distinct molecular and prognostic groups in therapy-related myeloid neoplasms.
abstract: Abstract Exposure to chemotherapy (CT) and/or radiotherapy increases the risk of therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MN), a heterogeneous group of disorders currently classified by treatment history rather than molecular features. Although germ line predisposition has been suggested in ∼20% of patients, its prevalence and clinical impact remain insufficiently defined. To address this, we analyzed 100 patients with t-MN by integrating clinical characteristics, prior treatment regimens, and genomic profiling. Somatic and germ line variants were identified using targeted next-generation sequencing (n = 33) or whole-exome sequencing (n = 67). Somatic abnormalities, including cytogenetic and/or molecular alterations, were detected in 89.8% of patients. Germ line variants were identified in 32.3% of patients, including mutations in cancer predisposition genes (19.8%) and myeloid disease-related genes (14.6%). Patient stratification by germ line landscape and gene category defined 2 prognostic scenarios and 3 subgroups with distinct clinical outcomes. Patients harboring germ line cancer predisposition variants were enriched for TP53 mutations and complex karyotypes and had an adverse prognosis. In contrast, patients with germ line myeloid-related variants and those without detectable germ line variants exhibited recurrent mutations in TET2, DNMT3A, SF3B1, SRSF2, RUNX1, and ASXL1, were associated with normal karyotypes, and had favorable outcomes. These findings underscore the importance of the germ line landscape in t-MN pathogenesis and support its incorporation into disease classification and risk stratification. Notably, CT exposure was associated with complex karyotypes and poor prognosis in patients with germ line cancer predisposition variants, highlighting a subgroup that may benefit from targeted surveillance and preventive strategies.

title: Prognosis and treatment-related toxicities in Down syndrome acute lymphoblastic leukemia in JCCG ALL-B12.
abstract: Children with Down syndrome (DS) have an increased risk of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Although recent reports describe some improvement, survival in DS-ALL remains inferior to that of non-DS-ALL. This study evaluated the prognosis, relapse patterns, and treatment-related toxicities of DS-ALL in the Japan Children's Cancer Group ALL-B12 trial, a nationwide prospective study using risk-adapted therapy. A total of 1,804 patients, including 44 DS-ALL, were analyzed. Risk classification used standardized criteria. The 5-year event-free survival and overall survival in DS-ALL were 70.5% and 81.8%, respectively, lower than 85.6% and 94.6% in non-DS-ALL (P < 0.001). Survival differences were most pronounced in standard-risk patients. DS-ALL showed fewer favorable genetics and relapse patterns dominated by isolated bone marrow events, with no CNS relapse. CRLF2 rearrangement was assessable in 43 of 44 DS-ALL cases; 15 of 43 (34.9%) were positive. In an exploratory analysis excluding canonical favorable or unfavorable subtypes (n = 36), the 5-year EFS in DS-ALL with and without CRLF2 rearrangement were 57.1% and 81.8%, respectively (P = 0.300), and the corresponding 5-year OS were 78.6% and 86.4%, respectively (P = 0.331). Treatment-related toxicities were more frequent in DS-ALL, including mucositis (27.3% vs. 7.1%), hyperglycemia (25.0% vs. 6.9%), and pulmonary infections (20.5% vs. 7.4%). Among DS-ALL patients with TP2 MRD ≥ 10-4 (n = 3), all relapsed and died within three years. No treatment-related death was recorded after induction, but one death of undetermined cause occurred. These findings highlight the continuing need to optimize DS-ALL therapy to reduce relapse and toxicity. UMIN CT Registry (UMIN000009339) and JCT (jRCTs041180101).

title: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis in a monogenic mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome.
abstract: Background Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE) is a rare, most often idiopathic fibrotic lung disease with poor prognosis, mainly affecting adults. Biallelic pathogenic variants in the deoxyguanosine kinase gene ( DGUOK ) cause a mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion syndrome, predominantly affecting infants with severe hepatic and neurological disease. Neither detailed pulmonary manifestations nor a pulmonary-dominant phenotype has been reported. Methods We describe nine patients with PPFE and DGUOK -associated mitochondriopathy. Clinical, radiological, histopathological, and genetic data were systematically collected from all patients. Functional studies, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNAseq), immunofluorescence staining, transmission electron microscopy, respiratory chain enzyme activity assays and mtDNA recovery experiment were conducted on patient-derived fibroblasts, muscle or lung tissues. mtDNA content quantification was performed on whole genome sequencing data. Results All patients (ages 5-36 years) carried biallelic pathogenic DGUOK variants, including an unreported intronic alteration in seven. All presented with progressive dyspnea, weight loss and some with pneumothoraces. Chest computed tomography and lung biopsies demonstrated features of PPFE. snRNAseq of lung tissue from four pediatric patients identified Aberrant Basaloid cells at the fibrotic edge, together with a transcriptional signature of nuclear DNA damage response. Ultrastructural analysis confirmed mitochondrial abnormalities in alveolar type 2 and Aberrant Basaloid cells. Conclusion This study provides evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction can contribute to early-onset PPFE independent of age, with a DNA damage response signature in aberrant epithelial cell populations previously described only in adult fibrotic lung disease. DGUOK deficiency and other hereditary mitochondrial disorders should be considered in children and young adults presenting with PPFE of unknown origin.

title: Interventions to increase participation in lung cancer screening programmes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyse the effectiveness of interventions in increasing informed choice and participation in lung cancer screening based on low-dose computed tomography (LDCT). Methods Five electronic databases, Medline (PubMed version), Embase, Cinahl (Ebsco version), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL, were searched for randomised controlled trials, nonrandomised controlled trials and before-after studies published from 2000 until 15 March 2023. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of interventions to increase rates of LDCT completion. Results Out of 3483 studies identified, 14 completed and 21 ongoing studies were included in the review. Shared-decision making (SDM)+navigation (OR 4.34, 95% CI 2.50-7.54) and outreach+navigation (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.70-2.84) resulted in a higher proportion of LDCT performed compared to the control group. Educational/informational interventions (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.19) as well as SDM alone (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.57-2.32) did not improve LDCT uptake, despite the second improving decisional outcomes in both intervention and control groups. Multicomponent interventions showed significantly higher LDCT uptake (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.79-3.90), compared to unicomponent interventions (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.14). The vast majority of interventions, including those in ongoing trials, are patient-oriented, while community-based, provider-level and system-level interventions remain rare. Conclusions Combining high-intensity patient-oriented interventions, such as patient navigation, active outreach and SDM, appears to be the most promising strategy to increase lung cancer screening uptake (low certainty of evidence). However, implementation studies are needed to evaluate interventions targeting both provider and healthcare systems level.

title: Geriatric respiratory medicine 2026: from artificial intelligence to personalised management of the multimorbid patient.
abstract: The profound demographic shift toward an ageing population has decisively moved the burden of chronic and acute lung diseases towards older adults, necessitating a transition from organ-centred models to integrated, multidimensional care. This review outlines a pragmatic framework for managing the complex interplay of immunosenescence, frailty and multimorbidity. In acute care, "pneumonia-associated sarcopenia" is identified as a critical driver of recurrent infections and functional decline, requiring a shift towards aspiration prevention and the aid of diagnostic tools such as lung ultrasound. The selection of noninvasive respiratory support, including high-flow nasal cannulas and noninvasive ventilation, must balance physiological efficacy with the risks of delirium and patient self-inflicted lung injury. Preventive strategies have evolved with the introduction of 20-valent pneumococcal and respiratory syncytial virus vaccines, alongside proactive screening for ɑ1-antitrypsin deficiency to enable precision interventions. Chronic disease management emphasises a "device-centric" inhalation therapy approach, tailoring delivery systems to impaired peak inspiratory flows and cognitive status rather than to pharmacology alone. The advent of biological therapies, particularly the use of dupilumab and mepolizumab in eosinophilic COPD, offers a transformative "steroid-sparing" effect, aiming for clinical stability and preserved independence. Finally, the integration of artificial intelligence as "augmented intelligence" and the "4Ms" multidisciplinary model (mentation, medication, mobility, morbidities) provide the necessary tools to navigate clinical complexity. This holistic strategy ensures that technological innovation remains anchored in patient-centred goals.

title: Artificial intelligence for automated lung nodule detection in chest computed tomography scans.
abstract: Automated detection of pulmonary nodules on computed tomography has evolved from rule-based image processing algorithms to sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) systems capable of nodule localisation, volumetric measurement and malignancy risk stratification. Four landmark papers published between 1994 and 1999 established the computational foundations of this field, introducing grey-level thresholding, morphological feature extraction, neural networks and three-dimensional analysis as core detection principles. We provide an overview of these foundational studies and trace the subsequent evolution of AI-based nodule detection, from early computer-aided detection systems to modern deep learning frameworks evaluated in the context of lung cancer screening programmes.

title: Development of 99m Tc-cefadroxil loaded chitosan nanoparticles as a novel radiotracer for detection of septic and aseptic foci.
abstract: Early detection of inflammation is critical for preventing disease progression, and nuclear medicine plays a pivotal role in this context. Imaging modalities such as single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) enable the early identification of functional abnormalities through the use of targeted radiotracers that specifically localize inflammatory processes. In this regard, antibiotic-loaded nanoparticles have emerged as a promising platform for inflammation imaging, integrating diagnostic capabilities with potential therapeutic functionality. Among these systems, chitosan-based nanocarriers (CS-NPs), a nano-polymeric pharmaceutical excipient, were employed for the encapsulation of the antibiotic cefadroxil (CDX). The formulation was prepared via a simple ionic gelation (cross-linking) technique. The physicochemical properties of the resulting nanoparticles were characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), zeta potential analysis, and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Drug encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity were subsequently quantified by UV-visible spectrophotometry. For imaging applications, CDX-loaded CS-NPs (400 µg) were radiolabeled with technetium-99m in the presence of stannous chloride (50 µg) as a reducing agent, yielding a complex with a radiochemical efficiency of 94 ± 1.3%. The resulting 99mTc-CDX-CS-NPs demonstrated excellent in vitro stability in fresh serum for up to 6 hours, which is suitable for diagnostic imaging applications. In vivo biodistribution studies in murine models of both septic and aseptic inflammation revealed significant tracer accumulation at infected and inflamed sites, with high target-to-non-target (T/NT) ratios of 8.55 and 6.02 after 2 hours post-injection, respectively. These findings suggest the developed radiotracer's ability to effectually localize septic and aseptic foci, irrespective of their underlying etiology.

title: Computed tomography-derived projected morphometry of four zygomatic sutures: distinct geometric profiles and bilateral agreement.
abstract: Background Zygomatic sutures are key landmarks in midfacial trauma, yet comparative data on their projected geometry and individual-level bilateral correspondence within a common computed tomography (CT) protocol remain limited. We compared the zygomaticomaxillary, sphenozygomatic, temporozygomatic and frontozygomatic sutures and assessed sex-, side- and age-related variation and bilateral agreement. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study analysed cranial CT examinations of 762 sides (total 381 adults). Projected length, end-to-end distance, sinuosity and angle to the Frankfort horizontal plane were measured bilaterally on standardised thick-slab maximum intensity projection reformats. Generalised estimating equations and patient-level Spearman correlations were used, with false discovery rate adjustment for multiple comparisons. Results The sutures had distinct dimensional, sinuosity and orientation profiles. Among the defined projected measurement courses, the zygomaticomaxillary suture showed the greatest mean length and end-to-end distance, and mean angles to the Frankfort horizontal plane ranged from 15.3° (frontozygomatic) to 67.1° (sphenozygomatic). Intersuture correlations were weak to moderate for dimensional and sinuosity parameters (largest ρ = 0.40). Angular correlations were small (largest absolute ρ = 0.12), and none remained significant after false discovery rate adjustment. Length and distance were greater in males for all sutures. Directional side differences were limited to sphenozygomatic straight-line distance, whereas individual bilateral agreement varied across sutures and parameters (bilateral intraclass correlation coefficients, 0.37-0.80). Conclusions The sutures showed distinct projected profiles, and small group-level side differences coexisted with variable individual bilateral agreement. These single-centre, single-scanner descriptive projected morphometric data require external validation and evaluation in fracture cohorts before use in reduction assessment or surgical planning.

title: Impact of reduced scan extent on tumor detection in 68 Ga-PSMA PET/CT for biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.
abstract: Background PSMA PET/CT plays an important role in biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (BCR-PCa). In general, PET/CT is performed as a limited or true whole-body examination. The majority of PET/CT scanners operate by measuring several bed positions or continuous motion with a limited axial field of view (FOV). Shortening the scan area thus results in a time saving, with unknown information loss regarding the detection of tumor manifestations. Methodology This retrospective single-center study included 200 patients with BCR-PCa after initial curative therapy who underwent a 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT scan from vertex to toe (true whole-body). Using retrospective subdivision into hypothetical partial body measurement protocols, the undetected tumor manifestations were examined. Classic PET/CT protocols were used: vertex to mid-thigh, skull base to mid-thigh, as well as CT-equivalent examination areas: chest/abdomen/pelvis (CAP), abdomen/pelvis (AP) and pelvis. Results Of 200 patients with a median PSA of 1.1 ng/mL, 128 (64%) showed at least one structural correlate of BCR-PCa in the true whole-body scan. The overall detection rate did not change for limited classic PET-protocols, or CAP measurements. CAP scans would not have detected all tumor manifestations in 16 patients (8%) and not all tumor-affected organ systems in six patients (3%), AP scans in 41 patients (21%) and 18 patients (9%), pelvic scans in 61 patients (31%) and 37 patients (19%), respectively. PSA may contribute to the prospective restriction of the scan area. Patients with PSA ≤ 0.75 ng/mL showed no diagnostic gain from whole-body imaging. This means that in 45% of patients in our cohort, a limitation to CAP scan would have been possible without losing information. Conclusions For a resource-saving use of routine PSMA-PET/CT, a scan from the vertex to the mid-thigh seems sufficient for detecting relevant metastases. For patients with low PSA levels, a more focused protocol that includes only the CAP region can be considered.

title: Lobar analysis of classical and deep learning radiomic features in chronic airflow limitation.
abstract: Background Quantitative chest computed tomography (CT) enables detailed assessment of structural lung abnormalities in chronic airflow limitation (CAL). We evaluated whether lobe-based classical radiomics and frozen deep learning transfer features from inspiratory and expiratory CT improved discrimination of CAL compared with handcrafted quantitative measures. Methods In this population-based study, 2,579 participants underwent inspiratory and expiratory CT and post-bronchodilator spirometry. CAL, defined as post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC < 0.70, was the primary modeling endpoint and was present in 430 participants; 2,149 participants without CAL served as controls. Lung lobes were segmented using nnU-Net. Classical radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics, and deep learning transfer features were obtained from frozen 3D U-Net and SegResNet encoders pretrained on the non-lung AbdomenAtlas dataset. A previously developed handcrafted feature set was included as a reference. Elastic-net regularized logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for classification, and performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Models based on expiratory features outperformed inspiratory-only models (AUC improvement 0.03-0.08). The best performance was achieved by classical radiomics combining inspiratory and expiratory features (AUC 0.87; positive predictive value 49%; negative predictive value 95%), exceeding the handcrafted model (AUC 0.81; PPV 34%; NPV 94%). Frozen transfer features from the non-lung-pretrained encoders showed slightly lower discrimination than classical radiomics, and combining feature types did not improve performance. Conclusion Lobe-based classical radiomics from combined inspiratory and expiratory CT improved cross-validated discrimination of spirometry-defined CAL in this population-based cohort, with expiratory imaging contributing substantially to optimal performance.

title: Non-Ischemic Cerebral Enhancing (NICE) lesions after flow diversion for intracranial aneurysms: a systematic review with case-level synthesis.
abstract: Background Non-ischemic cerebral enhancing (NICE) lesions are rare delayed inflammatory brain lesions reported after flow-diverter (FD) treatment of intracranial aneurysms. We systematically reviewed their reported incidence, clinical and imaging characteristics, diagnostic findings, management, and outcomes. Methods We performed a PROSPERO-registered systematic review. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched for reports of delayed NICE lesions after FD treatment of intracranial aneurysms that were not better explained by infarction or alternative causes. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Findings were synthesized narratively because heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Results Twenty-two studies met inclusion criteria; seven reported incidence data. One multicenter survey provided the only FD-specific denominator (12 NICE cases among 1201 FD-treated aneurysms; 1.0%), but the true incidence remains uncertain. Other estimates, using all aneurysm endovascular procedures as denominators, ranged from 0.05% to 1.3%. Overall, 40 unique FD-associated NICE patients were identified. Among cases with available individual data, median age was 54 years; all patients with reported sex were women, and all aneurysms with reported location involved the anterior circulation. NICE lesions appeared after a median of 73 days, most often with headache, focal deficits, or seizures, and as multifocal, predominantly ipsilateral enhancing lesions with edema on MRI. Brain biopsy was performed in six patients and identified hydrophilic polymer or other foreign material in four; in one additional case, device-coating detachment was observed directly. Both coated and uncoated FDs were represented, although the source component was usually undetermined. Systemic corticosteroids were administered in 22/24 cases with treatment data. Radiologic improvement or resolution occurred in 12/25, recurrent or fluctuating activity in 11/25, and 19/23 patients with reported functional outcomes were asymptomatic or independent at last follow-up. Conclusions Reported NICE lesions after flow diversion appear uncommon, but the true incidence remains uncertain. The available evidence supports a foreign-body inflammatory mechanism potentially related to hydrophilic coatings or other materials within the endovascular construct, without establishing a single culprit device. Corticosteroid-associated improvement is common, but relapsing or fluctuating courses require prolonged clinical and imaging follow-up. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD420251186127.

title: Prediction of death by neurologic criteria in patients with non-traumatic acute brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Robust predictors of death by neurologic criteria (DNC) after non-traumatic acute brain injury remain insufficiently defined. We therefore aimed to systematically synthesize the available evidence on prediction of DNC in non-traumatic brain injury. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched to August 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, observational studies, case series and registry data. Studies were included in the quantitative synthesis when sufficient comparable data for the same prognostic factor were available from at least two studies. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Results The database search identified 2,091 records. Eighteen studies comprising reported study cohorts of 9,070 participants were included. Quantitative synthesis included four studies (n=1,738), comprising two post-cardiac arrest and two stroke cohorts. In stroke populations, CT markers of severe intracranial mass effect were associated with a more than threefold increased odds of DNC (pooled OR 3.14, 95%CI 1.98-4.96; p<0.0001; I2=0%), while in post-cardiac arrest cohorts lower gray-white matter ratio values were associated with progression to DNC (pooled mean difference -0.15, 95%CI -0.22 to -0.07; p<0.001; I2=72%). Conclusions Evidence on predictors of DNC after non-traumatic acute brain injury remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous, with only a small number of studies providing robust analyses. Across these studies, CT-based markers - particularly indicators of diffuse cerebral edema or intracranial mass effect - show the most reproducible associations with progression to DNC.

title: Late enhancement and washout maps for distinguishing tumor progression from radiation necrosis in malignant brain tumors: an exploratory study.
abstract: Background Distinguishing between tumor progression and radiation necrosis during brain tumor follow-up is challenging. Advanced MR imaging techniques, such as perfusion, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and spectroscopy, can help differentiate between these conditions. In our clinic, we established a novel technique, the rapid washout and late-enhancement map. This study investigated the value of this map in distinguishing true progression from radiation necrosis. Methods Patients with a histologically confirmed initial diagnosis of glioblastoma, high-grade astrocytoma, primary central nervous system lymphoma, or brain metastasis who were undergoing radiochemotherapy and participated in our MRI protocol, including MR perfusion and rapid washout imaging, between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025, were included in the study. We volumetrically measured late enhancement and washout in brain tumors at all follow-up examinations and analyzed the resulting volumes. Additionally, we evaluated diffusion-weighted imaging and MR perfusion images. Results A total of 33 patients (25 with glioblastoma, two with astrocytoma grade 4, two with astrocytoma grade 3, one with CNS lymphoma, and three with brain metastasis) were included. Diagnostic confirmation was obtained by histopathological assessment in 20 patients, MRI follow-up in 13 patients, with additional fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography in two. Among these patients, 23 were diagnosed with tumor recurrence, four with mixed pathology comprising "radiation necrosis with scattered active tumor cells", and six with radiation necrosis. The mean washout ratio (± standard deviation) was 31 ± 18 % for progressive disease, 35 ± 20 % for mixed pathology, and 10 ± 7 % for radiation necrosis, respectively. Conclusions The washout ratio can enhance the differentiation between recurrent tumor growth and radiation necrosis during post-treatment monitoring of malignant brain tumors. As MR perfusion can yield inconclusive results in this setting, the proposed method offers complementary information that supports initial diagnostic decision making. Diagnostic discrimination may be strengthened by combining the relative cerebral blood volume with washout ratio analysis, rather than relying on a single imaging marker.

title: Optic disc and cup segmentation using Vision Mamba UNet with enhanced edge-guided attention in fundus images.
abstract: Background Glaucoma is an irreversible blinding disease for which early detection is essential. Precise segmentation of the optic disc (OD) and optic cup (OC) enables accurate cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) calculation, which serves as an important reference for glaucoma evaluation. However, the ambiguous boundaries between these structures make manual segmentation time-consuming and highly subjective. Methods This study proposes a hybrid framework for OD and OC segmentation in fundus images. The framework first adopts YOLOv10 to achieve coarse localization and extraction of the OD region, followed by fine-grained segmentation using the proposed EEGA-VMUNet network. Based on a Vision Mamba-UNet backbone, we design an enhanced edge-guided attention (EEGA) module to adaptively integrate multi-scale contextual information. This module strengthens the representation of edges and fine structural features. A multi-scale loss function is also used to improve robustness to scale variations. Results Experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that EEGA-VMUNet achieves competitive segmentation performance. On the same-domain test sets, OD Dice coefficients range from 95.20% to 97.65% and OC Dice coefficients range from 87.51% to 89.95%. Zero-shot cross-domain experiments achieve an OD Dice of 95.18% and an OC Dice of 85.13%. Conclusion The proposed model achieves competitive performance in both OD and OC segmentation tasks. Bland-Altman analysis suggests that the derived vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR) holds potential as a diagnostic aid for glaucoma screening, although its precision may require further improvement for longitudinal monitoring.
