title: Gastric Fungal Colonization as a Candidate Mechanism in ALS-Spectrum Motor Neuron Disease: A Hypothesis Supported by Five Years of Case Documentation
abstract: Background: The etiology of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) remains unknown in approximately 90% of cases [1]. A unified mechanism linking environmental mycotoxin exposure, gut-brain axis dysfunction, and motor neuron disease has not been systematically investigated. Hypothesis. Chronic colonization of the gastric mucosa by a mycotoxin-producing mold, concealed beneath a mucosal biofilm and therefore potentially undetectable by standard endoscopy, is proposed to drive sustained motor-neuron hyperexcitability through three concurrent mechanisms: (1) TLR activation on vagal afferent fibers projecting excitatory signals to brainstem motor nuclei via neural spill-over; (2) cross-reactive immune attack on motor-neuron surface proteins via molecular mimicry; and (3) Dectin-1-mediated neuroinflammation during biofilm disruption. Case. Five-year index case: five positive urinary Trichothecene assays including one after a 32-hour fast (internal source confirmed); six immunological assessments, including five CD25 measurements, showing markedly reduced measured T-cell activation markers and cytokine responses (CD25 1.0–3.1%, reference 13–24%; IFN-γ 79.5 pg/ml, reference ≥118; IL-17 5.4 pg/ml, reference ≥9.6); EMG-confirmed neurogenic remodeling followed by documented stabilization; over 30 reproducible pharmacological observations consistent with the proposed mechanism; and formal diagnostic exclusion across four institutions over three years. Implications. Convergent findings from the published literature, together with more than 30 internally consistent pharmacological observations, support formal investigation of the proposed model. Proposed initial investigations include urinary mycotoxin testing, lymphocyte transformation testing, mycotoxin antibody testing, visual contrast sensitivity screening, and biofilm-directed endoscopy with confocal laser endomicroscopy, targeted biopsy, and PCR analysis.

title: Biologically Inspired Selective Attention for Prostate MRI: A Segmentation-Guided Vision Transformer Framework for Computer-Aided Diagnosis
abstract: Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men, yet interpretation of multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) suffers from substantial inter-observer variability and depends on scarce expert radiologists. Expert readers follow a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine visual strategy: they first localize the prostate gland and then direct focused attention to tissue within it. Inspired by this biological selective-attention mechanism, we propose a segmentation-guided framework in which a modality-aware 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) first delineates the prostate gland from T2-weighted, ADC, and DWI volumes, and the resulting anatomical mask then constrains downstream cancer detection. Global self-attention models long-range anatomical context, analogous to the integration of peripheral and foveal information in human vision. Detection was evaluated through two pathways: gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features with classical classifiers, and a ViT classifier. On 200 patients from the public PROSTATEx cohort, the proposed segmentation model achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of [0.905] versus [0.831] for an optimized U-Net. The segmentation-guided ViT achieved an AUC of [0.987] and an accuracy of [0.998] for clinically significant cancer detection. Ablation experiments confirmed that anatomical guidance improved both pathways. These results show that emulating expert visual search strategies yields accurate and interpretable computer-aided prostate cancer diagnosis.

title: DeepSUM-DWI: A Joint Image Registration and Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network for Diffusion-Weighted MRI
abstract: Background: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is an important MRI technique for studying tissue microstructure and structural connectivity, but is limited by relatively low spatial resolution, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and sensitivity to inter-acquisition motion. A deep-learning framework was developed that jointly performs image registration and super-resolution on repeated low-resolution DWI inputs to generate a single registered, higher apparent spatial-resolution output. Methods: DeepSUM-DWI adapts a DeepSUM multi-image super-resolution architecture for repeated DWI. It comprises a shared 2D super-resolution feature extractor (SISRNet), a registration network (RegNet), and a 3D fusion network (FusionNet). Evaluation used (1) simulated repetitions with synthetic motion, (2) retrospectively downsampled acquisitions from 12 subjects, and (3) a prospective dual-resolution example with matched 1.0 × 1.0 and 2.0 × 2.0 mm² acquisitions. Results: DeepSUM-DWI reconstructed a single high-resolution-appearing DWI image from multiple low-resolution repetitions while preserving structural characteristics of the high-resolution acquisitions. The model remained robust across synthetic motion magnitudes. In retrospectively downsampled data, it improved NRMSE by 71–79% and PSNR by 10.6–13.5 dB, for super-resolution factors of 2–3, relative to averaging interpolated low-resolution images, with a mean SSIM > 0.99. In prospectively acquired data, it recovered finer structures than visible in the acquired low-resolution images while maintaining contrast consistency. Exploratory diffusion analysis suggested that some gains in apparent detail propagated to FA maps. Conclusions: DeepSUM-DWI provides a framework for joint registration and super-resolution of repeated DWI acquisitions, with potential to improve apparent spatial resolution while retaining the SNR benefits of repeated acquisition.

title: Biomechanical Evaluation of Uterine Morphology and Tissue Mechanical Properties in a Computational Model of the Pelvic Cavity
abstract: Female pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a gynecological disorder characterized by pelvic organ descent that significantly impacts quality of life. With increasing global burden, approaches for early diagnosis are essential. This study illustrates a patient-specific computational model of the pelvic cavity, updating the uterine and cervical geometric model and assigning cervical tissue properties. Three distinct uterine geometric models were assembled, based on literature measurements and magnetic resonance images for comparison and validation. Human cervical properties were extrapolated from biomechanical testing of ovine pelvic tissues. Finite elements simulations of the Valsalva maneuver were conducted to analyze the biomechanical effects of varying uterine morphology and tissue properties on the pelvic cavity, including the bladder neck, vagina, and uterosacral ligaments (USLs). Results show that a uterus with softer properties assigned exhibits less vertical displacement and relies more on USLs support than a stiffer one. Furthermore, uterine volume and morphology significantly influence pelvic dynamics: a larger uterus tends toward anteversion, while a smaller uterus increases vertical vaginal displacement (10.57 mm vs 6.04 mm) and requires greater USLs support. Anatomical variations directly constrain bladder neck displacement. These computational advancements aim to enhance patient-specific modeling, assisting clinical decision-making.

title: From Manual to Machine: Development and Internal Validation of an NLP-Based Prediction Model for Brain Death Using Admission CT Reports, 2011–2024
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Early identification of patients progressing toward brain death may reduce missed organ donation opportunities. We aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable natural language processing (NLP) model using admission brain computed tomog-raphy (CT) reports. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 163 adults ad-mitted between 2011 and 2024 with acute neurological injury; 96 subsequently fulfilled brain death criteria and 67 did not. Predictors were derived exclusively from admission CT report text using rule-based preprocessing and term frequency–inverse document frequency word 1–3-gram features. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine models were evaluated using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 20 repetitions. Vectorization, cal-ibration, model fitting, and threshold selection were restricted to training folds. A prespecified sensitivity target of at least 95% guided threshold selection. Interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). RESULTS: XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.807 (95% confidence in-terval, 0.793–0.820) and a pooled out-of-fold value of 0.791. At the high-sensitivity operating point, mean sensitivity was 0.947 and specificity was 0.275. SHAP identified clinically plausible descriptors related to cerebral edema, mass effect, ventricular distortion, ischemic injury, and midline abnormalities. CONCLUSIONS: Admission CT reports contain prognostic information that can be extracted using NLP to support earlier identification of patients at risk of progression to brain death and potential organ donation. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Study on the Value of pH-Responsive Probes in Evaluating Acidic Environment Changes During Chronic Liver Disease Progression in Rats
abstract: During the progression of chronic liver disease, changes in the acidic microenvironment of liver tissue are closely correlated with the extent of pathological injury, making precise monitoring of these changes critical for disease assessment. Traditional detection methods (e.g., blood gas analysis, tissue pH electrodes) suffer from limitations such as high invasiveness and low spatiotemporal resolution, hindering dynamic reflection of hepatic acid environment evolution. PH-responsive probes (e.g., fluorescent probes, magnetic resonance probes), leveraging their non-invasive, real-time, and high-specificity advantages, have emerged as a research focus in this field. This review focuses on the application of such probes in rat chronic liver disease models: outlining their design principles and types, analyzing their quantitative detection capabilities for liver acidification levels, summarizing their value in correlating pathological processes such as liver inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, and demonstrating their ability to identify disease progression and evaluate intervention efficacy through early detection of acidic environment changes. Studies indicate that pH-responsive probes provide a tool for elucidating the mechanisms of the acidic microenvironment in chronic liver disease and lay the foundation for developing non-invasive monitoring technologies in clinical translation, holding significant academic and practical value.

title: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.

title: Beyond the Classical Paradigm of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Evolving Phenotypes and the Role of Kidney Biopsy
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition encompassing distinct clinical and pathological phenotypes. Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate may follow divergent trajectories, with non-albuminuric kidney function decline representing a common and clinically relevant phenotype. Importantly, clinical features do not always reflect the underlying renal pathology, as patients with diabetes may present with diabetic kidney disease, non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD), or mixed lesions. Conventional clinical markers, including diabetic retinopathy, hematuria, proteinuria, and eGFR decline, modify but do not reliably establish the underlying diagnosis. Kidney biopsy therefore retains a selective but important role in patients with atypical or rapidly evolving presentations, particularly when histological findings may alter treatment or prognosis. Beyond diagnostic classification, biopsy can provide prognostic information through assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular injury. Future approaches should integrate longitudinal clinical trajectories with histopathology and molecular profiling, positioning kidney biopsy as a bridge toward mechanism-based classification and precision medicine in DKD.

title: Binary Classification of Breast Cancer Images Using CNNs Enhanced by ALO-CLAHE-MSER Preprocessing
abstract: This work presents an intelligent image-processing framework for automatically detecting and clas-sifying benign and malignant regions in breast tissue by integrating Contrast Limited Adaptive His-togram Equalization (CLAHE), Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER), and metaheuristic opti-mization algorithms. Identifying tumor-related regions in breast images is challenging because their visual characteristics can vary considerably with tissue density, illumination conditions, surface tex-ture, intensity distribution, lesion severity, and image acquisition conditions. These variations can make conventional image segmentation and manually configured MSER approaches sensitive to pa-rameter selection and less robust when detecting heterogeneous cancerous regions. To address these limitations, this study highlights the critical role of metaheuristic optimization as a key driver for fully automating and optimizing the combined CLAHE-MSER pipeline for binary breast cancer classifica-tion. Methods: First, CLAHE is applied to the input medical images to improve local contrast and enhance visual differences between healthy and cancerous tissue. The enhanced images are subse-quently processed using the MSER technique to identify stable intensity regions potentially associated with lesions or tumor masses. Rather than relying on manual configuration, the MSER parameter space and enhancement thresholds are formulated as a multidimensional optimization problem, and metaheuristic optimization algorithms are employed to automatically explore the parameter space and determine optimal configurations for region detection. Candidate solutions are iteratively evalu-ated using an objective function designed to improve the quality, stability, spatial coherence, and ac-curacy of the detected tumor regions prior to binary classification. The proposed metaheuristic-driven CLAHE-MSER framework therefore lets the detection process adapt automatically to the visual char-acteristics of individual medical images while eliminating dependence on manually selected parame-ters. Results: We performed experimental evaluations on medical images containing healthy, benign, and malignant regions. We quantitatively evaluated the performance of the proposed CLAHE-MSER framework, optimized by metaheuristic algorithms, using several image-quality, region-detection, and binary classification metrics. The experimental results indicate that incorporating CLAHE improves local contrast and facilitates the identification of subtle differences between healthy and affected tis-sue. Furthermore, metaheuristic optimization significantly improves MSER parameter selection, re-sulting in more consistent and spatially coherent detection of tumor regions than conventional MSER configurations and non-optimized approaches. The optimized configurations better preserve relevant cancer-related structures, maximizing overall binary classification accuracy while drastically reduc-ing the detection of healthy tissue and irrelevant regions. Conclusion: Integrating CLAHE- MSER, and metaheuristic optimization provides a robust, fully automated, and adaptive framework for binary breast cancer classification based on medical image analysis. CLAHE enhances the visual infor-mation needed to distinguish affected tissue, while MSER extracts stable image regions associated with potential tumor lesions. Metaheuristic optimization serves as the central component to automate and refine the detection process by dynamically identifying suitable parameter configurations for different image conditions. The proposed methodology represents a promising computational ap-proach for automated breast cancer screening, computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), lesion classification, and intelligent medical decision support systems.

title: Predictive Value of the Cincinnati Scale for Code Stroke Activation in Relation to CT Scan Findings
abstract: Background: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide and main cause of disability in adults. Timely care is essential to achieve reperfusion and preserve brain tissue. Efforts have been made to correlate CT signs with the Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale to activate the Comprehensive Stroke Protocol. Analyzing these factors may provide useful parameters for selection. Material and Methods: This analytical, cross-sectional, observational, prospective study was conducted at the Regional General Hospital in Orizaba, Mexico. A total of 497_20 non-contrast cranial CT scans were analyzed using PACS. Patients were followed through medical records until discharge diagnosis was confirmed. Data collection occurred from March 2024_45. Results: 497_2 CT scans were reviewed. The Stroke Code was most often used in the 70-79-year age group, with 56.9% female patients. Of 72_24 ischemic stroke cases, only 24_29 were within the therapeutic window. Conclusion: The Cincinnati scale as a rapid cerebrovascular screen has only moderate to low discriminatory ability. Sensitivity and positive predictive value are very low. Therefore, it is not suitable alone. The results provide opportunity to train doctors to use the Cincinnati scale alongside the NIHSS scale, which has better predictive ability. More public education is recommended to help patients present within the window.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Investigating Pseudo-Learning and Bias Propagation in MRI Brain Tumour Classification
abstract: A brain tumour is an abnormal growth of cells in the brain, which can be either benign (noncancerous) or malignant (cancerous). The 5-year survival rate for benign brain tumours is approximately 85-95%, whereas it is only 35-36% for malignant tumours. Therefore, early detection and diagnosis of brain tumours is important. The recent developments in deep learning have allowed for high precision, accuracy, and automation in detecting these tumours, including both gliomas and pituitary tumours. In this paper, three deep learning-based models for brain tumour categorisation from MRI images are compared to understand the limitations of accuracy-based evaluation with metrics such as class-wise performance and Grad-CAM. To assess the performance and observe various behavioural issues of the models used in this analysis, the MRI scans from the Brain Tumour MRI Dataset from Kaggle and the BRISC 2025 classification dataset containing MRI images from all four major tumour groups were leveraged for their training and testing. The first model serves as a baseline EfficientNet classifier, while the second model applies fine-tuning techniques to improve feature learning. The third model further enhances performance by incorporating multi-dataset training to increase data diversity. The reported confusion matrices show that Model V3 achieved 97.63% accuracy on its 800-image test set. Because its test set differs in size and may differ in composition from those of Models V1 and V2, this result should not be interpreted as a direct like-for-like comparison.The findings highlight the importance of combining conventional performance metrics with Grad-CAM analysis when investigating model behaviour, while further evaluation is needed to establish whether multi-dataset training reduces pseudo-learning or improves generalisation.
authorString: Gajbhiye LN, Kamble SS.

title: Beyond 99%: Auditing Leakage, Shortcuts and Calibration in COVID-19 CT Classification
abstract: Public CT benchmarks for COVID-19 report slice-level accuracy above 99%, yet slices from one scan are near-duplicates and most datasets ship without patient IDs. We audit a MobileNetV3-Large classifier on a 19,685-slice, three-class CT dataset (non-COVID, COVID, non-informative) along four axes: leakage, shortcuts, external validity and calibration. Replacing a random slice split with a group split on recovered pseudo-patients lowers accuracy from 99.42% to 97.18%, and to 95.39% when groups follow file order. The error rate rises 4.9 to 8.0 times, and recall of COVID slices falls from 99.6% to 96.0% and 88.8%. Scalar acquisition features alone reach 0.996 balanced accuracy under a slice split and 0.630 under a group split (chance 0.333), and models trained without the lungs, or with only the lungs, both reach about 93%. On two external sites, discrimination drops (AUROC 0.83 on Sao Paulo; 0.86 for COVID lesion slices against normal patients in Tehran), and every model scores community-acquired pneumonia as more COVID-like than COVID (AUROC 0.43 to 0.49). Calibration does not transfer: binary ECE rises from 0.02 in-domain to 0.19 to 0.53 externally, and temperature scaling recovers at most 0.034. Because the main dataset has no patient IDs, we tested our grouping against true IDs on the Tehran cohort. It recovers patients poorly (adjusted Rand index at most 0.29). A nearest-neighbor probe scores 0.998 under a random slice split, 0.551 under a true patient split and 0.717 under our recovered groups, so the slice-versus-group gaps we report are lower bounds on true patient-level leakage.

title: A Mask-Guided, Explainable Deep-Learning Framework with Verifiable Attention for Benign–Malignant Classification of Breast Ultrasound Images
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancer types in women, and reading a breast ultrasound is still very much dependent on the individual radiologist, creating inter-observer variability. Deep-learning classifiers can achieve accuracy comparable to that of experts, but there are two challenges for their use in routine practice: they rarely explain their predictions, and a model can reach the right label for the wrong reason, by attending to tissue unrelated to the lesion. This study addresses both of these. Methods: On the BUS-BRA dataset, we used the lesion segmentation mask as an additional input channel to the network, along with the RGB image, so two backbones (EfficientNet-B3 and EfficientNet-B4) were directed towards the lesion from the first layer, while only the initial convolution layer was modified, keeping the ImageNet-pretrained weights unchanged. To ensure a fair evaluation, the data were split at the patient level rather than the image level, preventing leakage. Training was performed with focal loss, heavy augmentation and test-time augmentation, with the decision threshold set on the validation set. Grad-CAM, SHAP, and Occlusion Sensitivity explained each prediction, and were scored for fidelity, stability, and overlap with the true lesion. Results: During the controlled ablation, the mask channel improved accuracy by more than eight points over an region-of-interest (ROI)-only baseline. The average of the two backbone models yielded 86.7% accuracy and 0.911 AUC on the held-out test set, and when applied to the independent BUSI dataset, without any modification, with the threshold frozen, it achieved 90.4% accuracy and 0.972 AUC, with Grad-CAM maps landing on the annotated lesions. Conclusions: The accuracy of mask guidance using an imbalance-aware design is competitive, and the accuracy can be transferred to an external dataset, providing a credible basis for decision support that can be verified by the clinician with the image.

title: Bridging AI-Assisted Cancer Screening and Public Health Surveillance: Evidence and Challenges in the Philippines (2020–2026)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping cancer screening globally, yet evidence supporting its clinical application and integration into public health systems remains limited in countries such as the Philippines. This narrative review synthesised documented Philippine applications of AI-assisted cancer screening from January 2020 to September 2026, examining their implications for cancer surveillance, health-system readiness, and policy. A structured review of scientific publications, government and health technology assessment documents, and grey literature revealed a limited and heterogeneous evidence base. Only two peer-reviewed studies reported separately identifiable Philippine patient data, both retrospective, addressing mammography classification and computer-aided colonoscopy. Multinational evaluations and reported commercial deployments suggested opportunities for AI-assisted detection but provided insufficient Philippine-specific evidence of clinical effectiveness and patient outcomes. No prospective validation studies in Filipino screening populations or local evaluations of AI-assisted cervical or liver cancer screening were identified. Beyond clinical validation, major barriers included predominantly opportunistic screening, incomplete population-based cancer registry implementation, fragmented digital infrastructure, workforce constraints, regulatory uncertainty, and insufficient economic evaluation. Recent national screening financing policies provide opportunities for integrating innovative technologies into established healthcare pathways. These findings underscore that the transition toward AI-assisted cancer screening requires not only technological advancement but also locally validated evidence, strengthened population-based surveillance, equitable access, and coordinated public health governance.
authorString: Subong BJJ.

title: Why fNIRS Still Lacks a General-Purpose Foundation Model, and What One Would Require
abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is almost absent from the foundation-model literature. On OpenNeuro, the largest open BIDS-structured neuroimaging repository, fNIRS accounts for 1.0% of participants and 1.6% of datasets, against 28.6 times more participants for EEG. We ask why, and what a first fNIRS foundation model would require. The paper is a review and a roadmap: its contribution is an inventory, a synthesis of evidence from adjacent modalities, and a set of requirements, not new model results.We argue that the barrier is not primarily data structure. The fNIRS data standards already require sensor positions to be recorded, so the laborious step of reconstructing where each sensor sat, which dominates the equivalent EEG models, is largely unnecessary here. The barrier is corpus scale, compounded by the absence of any clinical archive comparable to the Temple University Hospital EEG corpus, and by the recency of NIRS-BIDS, published in 2025 against 2019 for EEG. Because no single fNIRS corpus is large enough, aggregation across heterogeneous montages is the most plausible route to pretraining scale, which makes montage-agnostic architecture a precondition rather than an optimization.Reviewing four EEG foundation models that solve montage heterogeneity, we find that the two available ablations of both components rank spatial aggregation above the choice of positional encoding. Several models without a unifying spatial abstraction fall to near-chance under stringent cross-montage evaluation, mainly when encoders are frozen or tested on layouts they were not trained on. In hemodynamic and multimodal work, the one foundation model borrowed from another domain gave no uplift on fNIRS, while joint pretraining with EEG did. In the one available ablation, though, that benefit tracked the mutual information between modalities and, at the larger shot counts, fell below fNIRS-only pretraining at the lowest level tested. From functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) we take a direction fNIRS has not yet followed: recent work there has moved from signal reconstruction toward latent prediction, because the signal is noisy and off-the-shelf evaluation matters. That rationale may be particularly relevant to fNIRS, where some of the systemic physiological confounds, particularly the Mayer wave, overlap the band in which the hemodynamic signal is analyzed. We chart the nine fNIRS-relevant works we located. We identify three especially consequential properties of fNIRS with no electrophysiological counterpart (source–detector geometry, chromophore choice and hemodynamic timescale) and set out eight requirements for a first fNIRS foundation model, on which work is under way in our laboratory.

title: Evidential Safety-Gated Segmentation for Robust Brain Tumor Analysis with Missing MRI Modalities
abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation from multi-parametric MRI is indispensable for clinical decision-making, yet real-world deployment is persistently challenged by missing or corrupted modalities arising from scanner failures, protocol variations, and patient-specific contraindications. Existing models tend to fail silently under such conditions, propagating high-confidence but clinically incorrect predictions into downstream workflows. We present Fail-SafeAI, a safety-gated, uncertainty-driven framework that integrates evidential deep learning with a learnable clinical safety gate for reliable segmentation under modality absence. The backbone operates on the two most discriminative MRI channels — FLAIR and contrast-enhanced T1 (T1ce) — and is trained with aggressive per-channel dropout to build inherent robustness. Network outputs are parameterized as a Dirichlet distribution over four semantic classes, enabling direct epistemic uncertainty (vacuity) estimation in a single forward pass. At inference, the clinical safety gate evaluates per-slice uncertainty statistics and dynamically decides whether to accept the prediction, escalate to a radiologist, or trigger a lightweight conditional U-Net inpainter for missing channel synthesis. On BraTS 2020, Fail-SafeAI achieves a whole-tumor Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.864 under complete data and ≥0.795 under single-modality dropout, outperforming AdaMM by 7.2 percentage points under missing T1ce while reducing the Unsafe False Acceptance Rate from 5.1% to 0.2%. Uncertainty maps are demonstrably calibrated: vacuity is statistically higher for incorrect predictions than for correct ones, and the accuracy-rejection curve shows that deferring the 30% most uncertain pixels to a human expert raises retained accuracy from 68.8%

title: A Systematic Review of Tools for Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Classification
abstract: Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the common mental disorders affecting children and is often diagnosed with an important delay. This neurodevelopmental disorder is usually identified by symptoms such as a deficit in attention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness. There are clinical and data-oriented methods for ADHD diagnosis. Recently, artificial intelligence techniques for ADHD diagnosis have been taken into consideration. In this article, we have reviewed state-of-the-art deep learning and classical machine learning networks using a wide range of neuroimaging, neurosignal and related data, including structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), questionnaires, genome data, mo-tion data, performance tests and game simulation. In addition, we identified common validation methods and analyzed them. As an important aspect for clinicians, the brain regions of ADHD patients identified as discriminative by existing machine learning-based studies are investigated. In the end, we identify exiting research gaps, notably the lack of publicly available large-scale multimodal datasets, non-interpretability and inexplicability of many algorithms and the use of architectures that are unable to efficiently model the spatiotemporal features of the brain. Ultimately, we hope that researchers will implement explainable machine learning-based studies that use several neuroimaging modalities to aid clinicians in supporting their decisions for diagnosis, prognosis and for treatment planning.
authorString: Firouzi M, Fadaei S, Rashno A, Müller H.

title: A Robust and Explainable Radiomics Pipeline for Small Multimodal Datasets to Predict Metastasis in Patients with Soft Tissue Sarcoma
abstract: Preoperative radiotherapy and surgery are standard treatments for high-risk soft tissue sarcomas (STS), yet distant metastasis remains a significant clinical challenge. This study aims to develop a robust and interpretable multi-omics predictive model for metastasis, specifically addressing the limitations of small datasets. A retrospective analysis included 40 STS patients (23 with metastasis) treated with preoperative radiotherapy and surgery. Using PyRadiomics, 107 radiomic and dosiomic features were extracted from CT scans, dose distributions, and post-treatment contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI. A Logistic Regression classifier with L1 regularization was identified as optimal and rigorously evaluated via Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validation repeated 100 times. Single-modality models demonstrated limited predictive performance, yielding mean AUC-ROC values of 0.52 for CT, 0.59 for dose distribution, and 0.62 for normalized MRI. Integrating these features into a combined multi-omics signature substantially improved the mean AUC-ROC to 0.75. Furthermore, model explainability was ensured using Log-Odds to identify key predictive features. Combining anatomical, dosiomic, and MRI-derived features significantly enhances the prediction of metastatic relapse in STS patients. This interpretable approach shows strong potential for guiding personalized clinical treatments.

title: AI-Assisted Decision Support System for Radiologists in the Analysis of Chest X-Rays
abstract: This paper presents the development of a decision support system for diagnosing pa-thologies in chest X-ray images, based on artificial intelligence methods. The system accelerates primary diagnosis, reducing the workload on radiologists while ensuring high diagnostic accuracy through robustness to image artifacts and suboptimal image quality. The proposed solution includes preprocessing stages (CLAHE, DCP) and foreign object detection (YOLO, evaluated using ROC-AUC, IoU, and mAP metrics). To generate structured reports, the system integrates LLMs with RAG, leveraging clinical guide-lines and report templates. A user-friendly interface allows physicians to review and adjust the results of automated analysis before finalizing the diagnostic report. Keywords: chest radiography, AI-based diagnosis, detection, Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS), human-in-the-loop, AI assistant, computer vision, CNN, YOLO, treatment recommendation, RAG.

title: Overview of approved robotic systems for knee and hip arthroplasty: a narrative review.
abstract: Background and objective Robotic assistance in arthroplasty is now embedded in routine practice across many centres, yet information about which platforms are validated, what they can be used for legally, and how they differ technically is dispersed across regulatory notices and heterogeneous clinical reports. This narrative review synthesises PubMed-indexed evidence and primary regulatory sources to provide a comprehensive overview of currently approved systems for knee and hip arthroplasty. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched in August 2025 to identify relevant literature on approved robotic systems for knee and hip arthroplasty. Primary regulatory sources were also consulted to confirm approval status, indications, and technical characteristics. Key content and findings Architectures include active robots that autonomously mill bone, semi-active platforms that constrain surgeons' actions within haptic boundaries or guide saw cuts, and handheld solutions that add motorised control with real-time navigation. Imaging strategies span computed tomography-based planning, imageless intraoperative mapping, and fluoroscopy-guided registration in selected hip and knee applications. Most platforms are closed to the manufacturer's implant ecosystem, while a smaller group operates as open platforms with multi-implant compatibility. Across major markets, approvals are concentrated on total knee arthroplasty, with several systems also cleared for unicondylar knee arthroplasty and one imageless handheld platform carrying a specific indication for selected revision knee procedures. Background and objective

title: Evaluation and management of early hip osteoarthritis.
abstract: The early stages of hip osteoarthritis (OA) remain less clearly defined, particularly regarding the optimal therapeutic interventions to slow or prevent disease progression. This review synthesizes current evidence on the diagnosis and management of early hip OA, with an emphasis on hip preservation techniques. Initial management typically involves conservative measures, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), physical therapy, and corticosteroid injections. For select patients, modern surgical hip preservation techniques such as hip arthroscopy and peri-acetabular osteotomy (PAO) offer promising outcomes by preserving joint integrity and delaying or preventing the need for arthroplasty. Proper patient selection is critical for optimizing outcomes, with factors such as age, severity of arthritis, and baseline function influencing treatment success. Hip arthroscopy yields favorable results in patients with minimal joint space narrowing, Tönnis grade less than or equal to one, and mild chondral damage. PAO is most effective in younger patients with acetabular dysplasia and minimal arthritic changes. Although hip resurfacing arthroplasty remains an option for young, active male patients with good bone quality, concerns about complications have limited its use. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains the gold standard for advanced disease but may have less predictable outcomes in patients with minimal radiographic changes. Shared decision-making and thorough preoperative counseling are essential to set realistic patient expectations and guide treatment decisions. To that end, this review underscores the importance of a patient-centered approach in managing early hip OA to optimize outcomes and satisfaction.

title: Association of carotid atherosclerotic disease on ultrasound with functionally relevant coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study, a subanalysis of BASEL VIII.
abstract: Background Atherosclerosis is a systemic disease underlying coronary artery disease (CAD), and carotid atherosclerosis may serve as an accessible marker of systemic atherosclerotic burden. However, the diagnostic and prognostic relevance of carotid plaque characteristics in patients with suspected functionally relevant coronary artery disease (fCAD) remains uncertain. We aimed to investigate the association of carotid atherosclerotic plaque burden and morphology with fCAD and to evaluate the prognostic value of carotid plaque characteristics for future cardiovascular events. Methods This prospective diagnostic subanalysis of the BASEL VIII cohort included 430 consecutive patients evaluated for suspected fCAD at the University Hospital Basel, Switzerland, between October 2011 and February 2016. fCAD was determined by myocardial perfusion imaging using single-photon emission computed tomography, supplemented by coronary angiography and fractional flow reserve measurements when available. Carotid ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) were performed at enrollment to assess plaque presence, burden, stenosis severity, echogenicity, and intraplaque neovascularization. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death, were assessed during long-term follow-up using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results The study included 430 patients with suspected fCAD, of whom 105 (24.4%) were women. fCAD was confirmed in 136 patients (31.6%). Patients with fCAD more frequently exhibited carotid plaques than those without fCAD (78.7% vs. 68.0%, P=0.02). However, plaque burden, stenosis severity, plaque echogenicity, and intraplaque neovascularization were not significantly associated with fCAD. During 8 years of follow-up, 30 patients (7.0%) experienced non-fatal myocardial infarction, 17 (4.0%) suffered stroke, and 34 (7.9%) died from cardiovascular causes. The presence of carotid atherosclerotic disease was significantly associated with a higher risk of MACE [hazard ratio (HR) 2.69, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.33-5.45]. This association remained significant after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors and fCAD (HR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.09-4.42). In contrast, plaque morphology characteristics, including echogenicity and intraplaque neovascularization, did not provide additional diagnostic or prognostic value. Conclusions The presence of carotid atherosclerotic plaques was associated with fCAD and with an increased risk of future cardiovascular events in patients evaluated for suspected fCAD. However, carotid plaque burden, stenosis severity, echogenicity, and intraplaque neovascularization do not appear to improve the identification of fCAD or the prediction of long-term cardiovascular outcomes. In clinical practice, carotid plaque presence may provide complementary information on systemic atherosclerotic burden, whereas advanced carotid plaque characterization does not appear to add clinically relevant diagnostic or prognostic information in this patient population.

title: Deep learning radiomics model for lymph node metastases prediction: a diagnostic study.
abstract: Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) frequently exhibits lymph node (LN) metastasis, making early identification of high-risk patients crucial for optimizing treatment strategies. However, robust predictive models and external validation remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) model for preoperative detection of LN status in PDAC patients. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 233 pathologically confirmed PDAC patients from two high-volume pancreatic surgery centers between July 2015 and July 2022. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) scans and met strict inclusion and exclusion criteria. Two experienced radiologists independently reviewed imaging. Radiomics analysis was performed using MATLAB and Python-based PyRadiomics. Following feature selection, 14 radiomic features were retained to construct a radiomics score. Three predictive models were developed and compared. Results From 1,652 extracted radiomic features, 14 were selected to build a radiomics score significantly associated with LN metastasis (P<0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified tumor location, vascular invasion, white blood cell (WBC) count, platelet count, and radiomics score as independent predictors of LN metastasis, and a nomogram was generated. Various machine learning algorithms were evaluated to identify the optimal model combining radiomic and clinical data. Decision curve analysis demonstrated that the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model achieved superior accuracy and stability, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 in the training set and 0.81 in the validation set. Conclusions We successfully developed a LN metastasis prediction model integrating preoperative CT radiomics and clinical variables. The XGBoost-based model exhibited excellent accuracy, robustness, and generalizability. Future studies should focus on constructing more reliable models through standardized pathological sampling and prospective multicenter trials, alongside advancing imaging techniques to improve identification of small LNs.

title: Development and internal validation of a pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging-based radiomics prediction model for 1-year overall survival in treatment-naïve patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving transarterial chemoembolization combined with targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors.
abstract: Background Reliable pretreatment tools to identify treatment-naïve patients with intermediate-to-advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who may benefit from this combination are lacking. We developed and internally validated a clinical-radiomics model based on pretreatment T2-weighted fat-suppressed magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting 1-year overall survival (OS). Methods This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 85 treatment-naïve patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage B/C HCC treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors between December 2021 and April 2024. The last follow-up was April 1, 2026. The primary endpoint was 1-year OS status (death within 12 months vs. survival ≥12 months). Patients were randomly divided into a training set (70%) and a held-out test set (30%) using stratified sampling. Three-dimensional tumor volumes were manually segmented on pretreatment axial T2 spectral attenuated inversion recovery images. Features were first filtered for intra- and interobserver reproducibility, then selected using univariable screening and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression before being entered into the machine-learning models. The optimal model was selected via fivefold cross-validation in the training set and evaluated in a held-out test set through use of discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations. Results A total of 2,525 radiomics features were extracted, and four final predictors were retained: maximum tumor diameter and three filtered radiomics features. Gradient boosting machine (GBM) achieved the highest mean cross-validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) (0.818±0.079). In the held-out test set, the combined GBM model yielded an AUC of 0.91 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.87-0.93], accuracy of 84.6% (95% CI: 79.3-88.9%), sensitivity of 81.8% (95% CI: 72.2-89.0%), and specificity of 86.7% (95% CI: 79.1-92.1%); the Brier score was 0.04. Decision curve analysis suggested a net clinical benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. Conclusions A pretreatment T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI-based clinical-radiomics model demonstrated promising performance for predicting 1-year OS in treatment-naïve patients with BCLC stage B/C HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors. However, this single-center finding requires external validation before clinical implementation.

title: Dynamic instability is associated with worse patient-reported outcome measures after fusion for lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Dynamic instability is commonly considered when selecting surgical treatment for degenerative spondylolisthesis, which presents with a variety of radiographic morphology and severity. However, the relationship between dynamic instability and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) following fusion has been sparsely explored. This study evaluated if preoperative dynamic instability and other radiographic metrics were associated with PROs and perioperative outcomes following fusion for one-level lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis. Methods This retrospective study included adult patients undergoing surgical fusion for single-level lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis between 2010 and 2024 at a single, academic, urban medical center. Degenerative spondylolisthesis was identified utilizing lateral standing radiographs, and all radiographic metrics were evaluated by a team of six research fellows using standardized methods. Patients were eligible if they received either laminectomy with interbody fusion (IF) or laminectomy with posterior segmental fusion (LPSF). Patients receiving laminectomy alone were excluded, since no structural change can be accomplished. Multiple IF approaches were combined into the composite category due to insufficient subgroup sample sizes. Preoperative index level slip distance, foraminal height, disc height, segmental lordosis, index level facet joint angle and gap, pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis (PI-LL) mismatch, and dynamic instability greater than 4 mm at the index level based on flexion slip distance minus extension slip distance at the index level were recorded. Primary outcomes included PRO values of the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores collected from the final follow-up appointment in the electronic medical record; all PRO models adjusted for the corresponding baseline preoperative values from the immediate preoperative clinic visit. Other primary outcomes included intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL), hospital length-of-stay (LOS), and total opioid usage in the hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included any transfusions and complications. Multivariable linear and Firth logistic regression models were used to evaluate predictors of final PROs and clinical outcomes. Results Four hundred and seventy-three patients qualified for the study; 324 (68.5%) had available dynamic translation measurements and 140 (29.6%) had at least one complete pair of preoperative and final follow-up PROs. The mean follow-up time was approximately 15 months for patients who underwent LPSFs and 8 months for those who underwent IFs. Preoperative dynamic instability was associated with higher ODI [β=+15.14, 95% confidence interval (CI): 7.62 to 22.66, P<0.001] and VAS Back (β=+2.35, 95% CI: 1.16 to 3.54, P<0.001) scores than in patients without dynamic instability at final follow-up. Conclusions Most radiographic metrics were not associated with perioperative outcomes or PROs at final follow-up in degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis (DLS), but preoperative dynamic instability was identified as independently associated with worse PROs. However, the retrospective, single-center nature of the study as well as considerable missing follow-up data limit the ability of these findings to provide definitive comparisons of clinical effectiveness between treatment methods.

Preoperative index level slip distance, foraminal height, disc height, segmental lordosis, index level facet joint angle and gap, pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis (PI-LL) mismatch, and dynamic instability greater than 4 mm at the index level based on flexion slip distance minus extension slip distance at the index level were recorded. Primary outcomes included PRO values of the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores collected from the final follow-up appointment in the electronic medical record; all PRO models adjusted for the corresponding baseline preoperative values from the immediate preoperative clinic visit. Other primary outcomes included intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL), hospital length-of-stay (LOS), and total opioid usage in the hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included any transfusions and complications. Multivariable linear and Firth logistic regression models were used to evaluate predictors of final PROs and clinical outcomes.

Results

Four hundred and seventy-three patients qualified for the study; 324 (68.5%) had available dynamic translation measurements and 140 (29.6%) had at least one complete pair of preoperative and final follow-up PROs. The mean follow-up time was approximately 15 months for patients who underwent LPSFs and 8 months for those who underwent IFs. Preoperative dynamic instability was associated with higher ODI [β=+15.14, 95% confidence interval (CI): 7.62 to 22.66, P<0.001] and VAS Back (β=+2.35, 95% CI: 1.16 to 3.54, P<0.001) scores than in patients without dynamic instability at final follow-up.

Conclusions

Most radiographic metrics were not associated with perioperative outcomes or PROs at final follow-up in degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis (DLS), but preoperative dynamic instability was identified as independently associated with worse PROs. However, the retrospective, single-center nature of the study as well as considerable missing follow-up data limit the ability of these findings to provide definitive comparisons of clinical effectiveness between treatment methods.

title: Unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) posterior cervical foraminotomy utilizing intraoperative navigation: surgical technique.
abstract: Unilateral cervical radiculopathy is a common pathology seen by spine surgeons and can be treated in a variety of ways. Traditional operative management of unilateral radiculopathy caused by disc herniation(s) has consisted of anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), cervical disc arthroplasty (CDA), or posterior cervical foraminotomy (PCF). Each approach carries with it unique challenges and potential complications ranging from dysphagia to vascular injury, post-operative bleeding, non-union, subsidence, and significant pain. PCF is a well-established motion-preserving treatment for unilateral radiculopathy without myelopathy that avoids fusion-related adjacent-segment disease and approach-related dysphagia. Unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) is being increasingly utilized as an ultra-minimally invasive technique for decompression in the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine. Applications of UBE in the cervical spine continue to expand and have shown great promise in the treatment of cervical radiculopathy arising from disc herniations causing unilateral symptoms. UBE-PCF is safe and effective and has been shown to produce lower early post-operative neck pain, reduced blood loss, and shorter operative time than microscopic PCF. We present the case of a 36-year-old male with left-sided C8 radiculopathy resulting from a left C7-T1 disc herniation that was successfully treated with UBE-PCF. This procedure was performed with the use of intraoperative navigation for accurate portal placement and anatomy verification. We describe our indications, operating room setup, and surgical technique in detail.

title: When the safe triangle is unsafe: volumetric magnetic resonance imaging root mapping for patient-specific assessment of Kambin's triangle before transforaminal lumbar disc procedures.
abstract: Background Kambin's triangle is a useful geometric model for lumbar transforaminal access, but the clinically usable corridor is patient specific because the exiting nerve root, dorsal root ganglion (DRG), traversing neural structures, anatomic variants, and disease-related displacement may alter the contemplated path. We evaluated volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) root mapping as a method for characterizing nerve-root anatomy relevant to patient-specific transforaminal trajectory planning. Methods This retrospective descriptive MRI-anatomy study analyzed 76 selected patients who underwent volumetric 3D T2-weighted MRI root mapping between March 1, 2022 and March 12, 2026 during evaluation of symptomatic lumbar levels before contemplated transforaminal or percutaneous disc access. Sixteen earlier contrast-assisted cases are mentioned only as historical technique-development context and were not included in the MRI analysis. Multiplanar, oblique, and curved reconstructions were reviewed collaboratively by a radiologist with musculoskeletal/spine imaging involvement and the operating surgeon/radiology team. Trajectory assessment distinguished anatomically favorable, borderline, and unfavorable/high-risk relationships, including dimensional incompatibility and direct neural trajectory conflict. Results Nine of the 76 patients (11.8%) demonstrated one of the two predefined nerve-root findings relevant to the intended transforaminal trajectory. Four unique patients had double or variant nerve roots occupying the intended Kambin corridor. Five additional unique patients had displacement of the exiting nerve root into the planned cannula trajectory; three were considered unfavorable/high-risk and two borderline. The two groups did not overlap. The abnormalities were identified at L4-5 in five patients, L5-S1 in three, and L3-4 in one. The remaining 67 patients did not demonstrate either predefined finding and are not interpreted as a validated safe comparator group. None of the nine relevant cases generated a material disagreement regarding the root-course abnormality or its relationship to the contemplated trajectory. Conclusions Volumetric MRI may identify patient-specific neural anatomy relevant to transforaminal trajectory and route planning. Its contribution is trajectory-oriented visualization rather than proof of procedural safety or diagnostic superiority over routine MRI. The observed frequency in this selected symptomatic-level cohort is descriptive and should not be interpreted as the population prevalence of aberrant nerve-root anatomy.

title: Clinical and prognostic characteristics of concurrent small cell lung cancer in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Lung cancer (LC) is a comorbidity that seriously affects the prognosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. Small cell LC (SCLC) accounts for the highest proportion of hospitalized LC patients with concurrent IPF at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH). To enable effective and standardized management of patients with IPF and SCLC, this study aims to summarize the clinical and prognostic characteristics of IPF-SCLC patients to improve their prognosis. Methods We retrospectively enrolled patients with IPF (diagnosed by 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT criteria)-SCLC (pathologically confirmed) admitted to PUMCH from January 2014 to December 2023. Clinical manifestation, chest computed tomography (CT) imaging, laboratory test, treatment and outcome data of patients with IPF-SCLC were collected and reviewed in detail with final follow-up on June 30, 2024. Results Forty patients with IPF-SCLC were included with the average age of 68.2±6.3 years (range, 54 to 82 years). And there were 37 (92.5%) males. Median follow-up time was 12.0 months. Additionally, 35 (87.5%) patients had a smoking history. Twenty-eight (70.0%) IPF-SCLC patients were concurrent with one or more other underlying diseases. Emphysema was detected in 26 (65%) patients via chest CT. IPF and SCLC were diagnosed during the same period in 23 (57.5%) patients, whereas SCLC was diagnosed during the follow-up of IPF in the remaining 17 patients. However, pirfenidone and nintedanib were only prescribed to two patients, respectively. Most patients were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC: 17 (42.5%) patients had stage IV SCLC, and 15 (37.5%) patients had stage III SCLC. Furthermore, with respect to anticancer therapy, one (2.5%) patient received no chemotherapy, 2 (5%) patients received oral etoposide, 37 (92.5%) patients received intravenous chemotherapy, and 11 (27.5%) patients received pulmonary radiotherapy. Finally, 29 (72.5%) patients died during follow-up. The main causes of death were acute exacerbation of IPF (AE-IPF) (13 patients, 44.8%) and progression of SCLC (12 patients, 41.4%). Conclusions The patients with IPF-SCLC included in our studies were mainly elderly males with a heavy smoking index, most of whom were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC. Antifibrotic medications for IPF were uncommon, and chemotherapy was the main cancer treatment. The progression of uncontrolled SCLC and AE-IPF were the main causes of death. Clinicians should consider early initiation of antifibrotic therapy alongside chemotherapy, monitor for the occurrence of AE-IPF, and adopt multidisciplinary management.

title: Clinical and prognostic analysis of unicentric mediastinal Castleman disease: a 10-year retrospective series study.
abstract: Background Castleman disease (CD) is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder, and unicentric mediastinal CD (UMCD) represents an uncommon thoracic manifestation for which surgical resection remains the mainstay of treatment.This study aims to: (I) characterize the anatomical distribution of UMCD in a single-center cohort; (II) evaluate the efficacy of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for UMCD resection and identify preoperative predictors of thoracotomy; (III) analyze prognostic outcomes in surgically managed UMCD patients. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 49 consecutive UMCD patients (26 males, 23 females; mean age 37.27±15.27 years) undergoing surgical resection at the department of thoracic surgery (Tangdu Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University) between May 2014 and October 2024. Demographic characteristics, anatomical distributions, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. Comparative analysis between VATS and thoracotomy groups was performed using independent samples t-tests. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of thoracotomy, with diagnostic performance evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier methodology. Results The most frequent anatomical involvement occurred in station 3A lymph nodes (12 cases, 24.5%), followed by station 10 (11 cases, 22.3%) and station 4 (8 cases, 16.3%). Mean tumor size was 6.25±3.09 cm (intraoperative measurement). Histopathological subtypes included hyaline vascular variant (43 cases, 87.7%), plasma cell variant (4 cases, 8.2%), and mixed-type (2 cases, 4.1%). Compared to thoracotomy, VATS demonstrated shorter operative duration (P<0.05), reduced intraoperative blood loss (P<0.05), and shorter postoperative chest tube retention (3±2.81 vs. 5.52±3.54 days, P<0.05). Multivariate analysis identified tumor diameter >6.6 cm (P<0.05) and arterial-phase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) attenuation >102 Hounsfield units (HU) (P<0.05) as independent predictors of thoracotomy. ROC analysis revealed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.875 for the combined diagnostic model. With a median follow-up duration of 52 months, the VATS group maintained 100% recurrence-free survival. In the thoracotomy group, three patients succumbed to disease (two from local recurrence refractory to conservative therapy, one from postoperative pneumonia with respiratory failure following pneumonectomy). The overall survival (OS) rate for the cohort was 91.83%. Conclusions Station 3A lymph nodes represent the predominant anatomical site of UMCD involvement. VATS resection confers significant advantages over thoracotomy, including reduced operative time, blood loss, and postoperative recovery duration. The diameter >6.6 cm and arterial-phase CT attenuation >102 HU of tumors serve as reliable preoperative indicators for thoracotomy. Early surgical intervention correlates with favorable prognosis, while postoperative complications and local recurrence demonstrate significant association with mortality.

title: Investigating the correlation between temporalis, masseter and cervical muscle mass on a single cross-sectional image.
abstract: Background Low skeletal muscle mass (SMM) is an established prognostic factor in oncology and is conventionally quantified at the third lumbar vertebra. In brain tumour patients, abdominal imaging is seldom available, and craniofacial measurements from routine brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), temporalis muscle thickness (TMT) and masseter cross-sectional area (MCSA), have been proposed as alternatives. Whether these measurements can substitute for one another, or for cervical [skeletal muscle area at the third vertebra (C3SMA)] and lumbar muscle mass, is unknown. We investigated the correlation and classification agreement between these measurements. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 247 patients who underwent awake craniotomy at Amsterdam University Medical Center between 2003 and 2020. TMT, MCSA and C3SMA were measured on pre-operative three-dimensional (3D) T1-weighted MRI, and L3 skeletal muscle area (L3SMA) and index (L3SMI) were estimated from C3SMA using a previously established method. TMT was available in 247 patients, MCSA in 239 and C3SMA in 136. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation coefficients, crude and adjusted for body mass index (BMI) and, separately, for age and sex. Low SMM was classified using established cut-off values for TMT (≤6.3 mm in men, ≤5.2 mm in women) and L3SMI (<43.2 cm 2 /m 2 ) and, as no validated masseter threshold exists, the sex-specific lowest quartile for MCSA. Agreement between classifications was assessed using Cohen kappa and interobserver reliability using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Results All pairwise correlations were low: TMT and MCSA r=0.39 (P<0.05, n=239), MCSA and C3SMA r=0.30 (P<0.05, n=136), TMT and estimated L3SMA r=0.24 (P<0.05, n=136) and TMT and C3SMA r=0.20 (P<0.05, n=136). Adjustment for BMI altered the coefficients minimally (TMT and MCSA r=0.37, P<0.001), whereas adjustment for age and sex rendered the association between MCSA and C3SMA non-significant (r=0.11, P=0.20). Among the 136 patients with all three measurements, agreement in classifying low SMM was poor using the thresholds applied (Cohen kappa 0.11 for TMT versus MCSA, 0.07 for MCSA versus L3SMI and 0.01 for TMT versus L3SMI), and only 2 patients (1.5%) were concurrently classified as having low SMM by all three measurements. Interobserver reliability was excellent [ICC 0.919, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.790-0.969 for TMT; ICC 0.987, 95% CI: 0.967-0.995 for MCSA]. Conclusions Craniofacial, cervical and estimated lumbar muscle measurements showed low correlations with one another and poor agreement in classifying low SMM using the thresholds applied in this study. As L3SMI was estimated rather than directly measured, non-interchangeability cannot be definitively established, but these findings provide little support for using craniofacial measurements as substitutes for one another or for cervical and lumbar muscle mass.

Among the 136 patients with all three measurements, agreement in classifying low SMM was poor using the thresholds applied (Cohen kappa 0.11 for TMT versus MCSA, 0.07 for MCSA versus L3SMI and 0.01 for TMT versus L3SMI), and only 2 patients (1.5%) were concurrently classified as having low SMM by all three measurements. Interobserver reliability was excellent [ICC 0.919, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.790-0.969 for TMT; ICC 0.987, 95% CI: 0.967-0.995 for MCSA].

Conclusions

Craniofacial, cervical and estimated lumbar muscle measurements showed low correlations with one another and poor agreement in classifying low SMM using the thresholds applied in this study. As L3SMI was estimated rather than directly measured, non-interchangeability cannot be definitively established, but these findings provide little support for using craniofacial measurements as substitutes for one another or for cervical and lumbar muscle mass.

title: Quantitative coronary plaque characteristics on coronary computed tomography angiography and their prognostic value in patients with chronic kidney disease.
abstract: Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events. This study compared coronary plaque characteristics assessed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) between patients with and without CKD and evaluated their associations with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Methods This secondary analysis of the multicenter CREATION-CHINA cohort included patients with suspected coronary artery disease who underwent CCTA during 2016-2020. CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m 2 . Propensity score matching (1:3) used age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, smoking, family history of coronary artery disease, and hyperlipidemia. Quantitative plaque characteristics and perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI) were assessed. MACE comprised all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization >90 days after CCTA. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs); analyses of CCTA-derived predictors were adjusted for age, body mass index, and hypertension. High plaque burden was defined as total plaque burden in the highest quartile. Results After matching, 2,267 patients were included (588 with CKD and 1,679 without CKD). During a median follow-up of 3.47 years (interquartile range, 2.36-4.10), MACE occurred in 30 patients with CKD (5.1%) and 52 without CKD (3.1%; P=0.035). Patients with CKD had higher median total plaque volume (39.90 vs. 0 mm 3 ), median total plaque burden (8.83% vs. 0%), and prevalence of high-risk plaque (9.35% vs. 4.35%; all P<0.001). Among patients with CKD, lipid plaque burden (adjusted HR =1.107, 95% CI: 1.006-1.218; P=0.038) and high FAI (adjusted HR =4.027, 95% CI: 2.329-6.960; P<0.001) were independently associated with MACE. Compared with patients without CKD and with low plaque burden, those with CKD and high plaque burden had a higher risk of MACE (adjusted HR =6.153, 95% CI: 2.937-12.890; P<0.001). Conclusions CKD was associated with greater coronary plaque burden and a higher incidence of MACE. Lipid plaque burden and high FAI were independently associated with MACE after adjustment for age, body mass index, and hypertension, supporting their potential role in cardiovascular risk assessment in patients with CKD.

title: Radiomics-augmented lesion characterization on prostate multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging: first-order features and ratio metrics may improve diagnostic performance in prostate cancer.
abstract: Background Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) is increasingly recognized as an important diagnostic modality in the evaluation of prostate cancer. This analysis sought to investigate whether simple, ratio-normalized quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) biomarkers obtained from routine mpMRI of the prostate provide incremental diagnostic value beyond the Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System version 2.1 (PI-RADS v2.1) for the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). Methods In this retrospective single-center study, 129 men underwent pre-biopsy 3-Tesla mpMRI followed by MRI/ultrasound fusion-guided biopsy. Quantitative first-order imaging features representing the three principal imaging domains underlying PI-RADS were derived from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging and normalized to intra-patient reference tissue. The analyses were performed on a lesion-specific basis and stratified by anatomical zone. Zone-specific logistic regression models were constructed to assess the incremental diagnostic value of quantitative biomarkers beyond PI-RADS v2.1. Results In the peripheral zone (PZ; 99 lesions), PI-RADS alone exhibited moderate discrimination for csPCa [area under the curve (AUC) =0.723]. An integrative model combining PI-RADS with prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD) and quantitative MRI-derived ratios from DWI, T2WI, and DCE significantly improved discrimination [AUC =0.901, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.839-0.964]. After bootstrap-based optimism correction, the AUC decreased to 0.879. In the transition zone (TZ; 30 lesions), univariable analyses revealed no consistent differences in quantitative parameters between clinically significant and non-clinically significant lesions. PI-RADS alone yielded an AUC of 0.670, while ratio-based quantitative parameters did not provide meaningful incremental diagnostic value beyond PI-RADS v2.1. Conclusions Simple, ratio-normalized quantitative MRI parameters integrated with PI-RADS and PSAD showed potential incremental value for detecting csPCa in the PZ. Conversely, these parameters demonstrated no statistically significant incremental diagnostic value beyond PI-RADS in the TZ in this limited cohort. These findings support a zone-aware, pragmatic approach to the quantitative augmentation of PI-RADS using routinely available MRI metrics.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based quantitative assessment of fatty infiltration in skeletal muscle and myocardium: a narrative review of technical principles, differences in clinical applications, and future directions.
abstract: Background and objective Fatty infiltration of skeletal muscle and myocardium is associated with muscle dysfunction, myocardial fibrosis, and arrhythmias. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based fat quantification techniques are being increasingly applied in the skeletal muscle and myocardium, but no review has systematically compared measurements in these areas. The purpose of this review was to compare the quantification of skeletal muscle and myocardial fat in terms of technical principles, clinical applications, and research paradigms. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, relevant journal databases, and conference proceedings (e.g., Proceedings of the International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine) were searched up to December 2025 for English-language literature with the following keywords: "MRI", "fat quantification", "Dixon", "magnetic resonance spectroscopy", "T1 mapping", "T2 mapping", "skeletal muscle", "myocardium", "epicardial adipose tissue", and "artificial intelligence". Original research, reviews, and consensus statements were included. Key content and findings Literature onthe Dixon method, magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), mapping techniques, magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF), and artificial intelligence (AI) was summarized. In skeletal muscle, the Dixon method is the practical standard, demonstrating robust multicenter reproducibility and established functional correlations in muscular dystrophy, sarcopenia, and inflammatory myopathies. In the myocardium, fat quantification relies mainly on mapping techniques, especially T1 mapping and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) quantification, as Dixon and MRS techniques are limited by cardiac motion, thin walls, and low-fat content. Myocardial mapping detects subclinical injury, and increased EAT volume is independently associated with myocardial fibrosis. These techniques aid diagnosis and risk stratification in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, diabetic cardiomyopathy, and Fabry disease. AI is driving automated segmentation and prognostic prediction in both fields. Conclusions Skeletal muscle fat quantification is predominantly conducted with the Dixon method and is relatively mature, whereas myocardial fat quantification relies mainly on mapping techniques and lacks standardization. The multicenter validation of approaches related to skeletal muscle and related experiences in automated segmentation and AI application can inform practices in the quantification of myocardial fat. Combined cardiac-skeletal muscle assessment and integrated multiparametric imaging are promising future directions in the broader field.

title: Lacrimal gland volume changes in unilateral lacrimal drainage obstruction and anophthalmic sockets: a retrospective computed tomography volumetric study.
abstract: Background The lacrimal gland (LG), ocular surface, and lacrimal drainage system form an integrated lacrimal functional unit (LFU) that contributes to ocular surface homeostasis. Research on whether lacrimal drainage obstruction (LDO) or an anophthalmic socket is associated with measurable changes in LG volume is limited. This study aimed to evaluate LG volume changes in patients with unilateral LDO or a unilateral anophthalmic socket and to assess whether these structural changes are consistent with altered regulation in the LFU. Methods In this retrospective comparative computed tomography (CT) volumetric study, bilateral LG volumes were measured in 11 patients with unilateral congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (CNLDO), 40 patients with unilateral primary acquired nasolacrimal duct obstruction (PANDO), 24 patients with a unilateral anophthalmic socket, and age-matched imaging controls. LG volumes were compared between the affected side, the contralateral side, and the corresponding control groups. Associations between disease duration and ipsilateral LG volume were assessed using Spearman correlation. Results Affected-side LG volumes were significantly reduced compared with both the contralateral sides and controls in patients with CNLDO (481.8±164.3 vs. 591.3±172.7 and 631.4±136.7 mm 3 ; P<0.001 and P=0.011), PANDO (399.1±107.5 vs. 465.7±116.5 and 502.8±121.7 mm 3 ; both P<0.001), and an anophthalmic socket (434.9±68.9 vs. 512.0±95.6 mm 3 , P=0.003; vs. controls, P=0.032). Disease duration was negatively correlated with ipsilateral LG volume in PANDO (r=-0.392, P=0.013) and anophthalmic (r=-0.410, P=0.046) patients. Conclusions Unilateral LDO and anophthalmic socket were associated with reduced ipsilateral LG volume compared with both the contralateral side and corresponding controls. Longer disease duration was negatively correlated with ipsilateral LG volume in patients with PANDO and in patients with an anophthalmic socket. These findings suggest that LG morphology may reflect chronic alterations in tear drainage and ocular surface sensory input in the LFU, although the underlying neural mechanisms require further investigation.
