title: Deep learning-based super-resolution ultrashort echo time MRI combined with free-breathing Star-VIBE dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI for characterization of Lung-RADS 4 pulmonary nodules.
abstract: Background Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) 4 pulmonary nodules require further evaluation because of indeterminate malignancy risk. However, repeated computed tomography (CT) examinations raise concerns about cumulative radiation exposure, and ultrashort echo time magnetic resonance imaging (UTE-MRI) remains limited by spatial resolution and motion sensitivity. This study aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of generative adversarial network (GAN)-based super-resolution UTE MRI (SR-UTE-MRI) in combination with star-volumetric interpolated breath hold examination (Star-VIBE) dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) for such nodules, using CT and histopathological findings as reference standards. Methods In this prospective study, patients with Lung-RADS 4 pulmonary nodules underwent CT, free-breathing UTE-MRI with subsequent SR reconstruction, and Star-VIBE DCE-MRI. Nodule size, morphological features, and perfusion parameters were assessed. Diagnostic performance of individual imaging metrics and a combined model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. A total of 91 patients (43 men and 48 women; mean age, 56.2±13.9 years) with 91 nodules (27 part-solid and 64 solid; mean diameter, 24.1±8.9 mm) were finally included. Results Measurements derived from UTE-MRI underestimated mean nodule diameter relative to CT, resulting in misclassification in a subset of nodules. SR-UTE-MRI images reduced measurement bias and improved Lung-RADS classification accuracy and visualization of morphological features. Malignant pulmonary nodules demonstrated significantly higher volume transfer constant (K trans ) and rate constant (K ep ) values compared with benign nodules (K trans : 0.28 ± 0.19 min -1 vs. 0.16±0.11 min -1 , P<0.001; K ep : 0.79±0.38 min -1 vs. 0.53±0.23 min -1 ,P<0.001). Among individual parameters, K trans exhibited the highest diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) =0.799; cut-off, 0.14 min -1 ]. A multiparametric model incorporating perfusion parameters, nodule size, and spiculation yielded superior discriminatory performance (AUC =0.946; sensitivity =91%; specificity =88%; accuracy =90%). Conclusions GAN-based SR-UTE reduced the underestimation of lesion size associated with UTE-MRI and improved the accuracy of Lung-RADS classification. Star-VIBE DCE-MRI provided quantitative functional biomarkers for the assessment of malignancy. The integration of structural and functional imaging parameters yielded superior diagnostic performance compared with single-modality or single-parameter approaches, highlighting its potential as a comprehensive, non-ionizing imaging strategy for evaluation of indeterminate pulmonary nodules.

title: Evaluation of virtual monochromatic imaging combined with metal artifact reduction in low-dose dual-energy computed tomography: a phantom study.
abstract: Background Metal implants can cause substantial artifacts on computed tomography (CT), and the optimal virtual monochromatic (VM) energy for metal artifact reduction (MAR) remains uncertain. This study assessed metal-artifact reduction and overall image quality on low-dose dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) VM images reconstructed with Smart MAR. Methods A multi-energy CT phantom (GPH-75B; Kyoto Kagaku Co., Ltd., Kyoto, Japan) was scanned in DECT mode with a 12-mm titanium rod positioned at the center, right, and superior portions. VM images from 40 to 140 keV were reconstructed with MAR and without MAR (no-MAR). Image quality was assessed according to artifact and structure visibility scores, CT values, standard deviations (SDs), titanium-rod dimensions, structural similarity index (SSIM), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and root mean square error (RMSE). MAR and no-MAR measurements were compared via two-sided paired t-tests. Results Across the three titanium-rod positions, MAR generally reduced artifacts, improved titanium-rod edge visibility, and reduced geometric distortion compared with no-MAR. At every rod position and energy level, MAR yielded higher SSIM and PSNR and lower RMSE compared to no-MAR (all P values <0.05). At the central position, the transverse-to-longitudinal diameter ratio was 0.94-1.03 with MAR and 0.21-0.81 with no-MAR (all P values <0.001), remaining close to 1.0 at energies ≥60 keV with MAR. For MAR images, adjacent-structure clarity was highest at 60 keV. In both groups, SSIM and PSNR increased with increasing energy, whereas RMSE and image noise decreased. Conclusions MAR consistently improved image quality across titanium-rod positions. In terms of artifact reduction, implant depiction, and adjacent-structure visibility, 60 to 80-keV VM images with MAR provided the most favorable overall performance under the tested low-dose conditions.

title: Quantitative analysis of motion-induced dose uncertainty and robust optimization in liver lattice radiotherapy: a comparative study.
abstract: Background The precise delivery of high doses to lattice vertices in liver lattice radiotherapy (LRT) can be compromised by respiratory motion.This study aimed to quantitatively characterize the dosimetric impact of respiratory motion on liver LRT and to assess the potential of four-dimensional (4D) robust optimization in mitigating motion-induced uncertainties. Methods Twenty-one patients with bulky liver tumors underwent 4D computed tomography scanning. Three lattice target volumes (LTVs) were generated using varied lattice geometries defined by vertex sizes and spacing. Conventional and 4D robust plans were generated on average intensity projection images. Four-dimensional dose distributions were reconstructed via deformable image registration-based dose accumulation across all respiratory phases. Dosimetric parameters of LTVs and organs at risk (OARs) were compared between static three-dimensional (3D) and dynamic 4D scenarios. Spearman correlation coefficients were calculated to quantify the relationship between motion amplitudes and dosimetric variations. Results Respiratory motion introduced substantial dose degradation in conventional plans. Specifically, LTV D min and D 98 , which represent the minimum dose and the dose covering 98% of the structure, decreased by up to 12.71% and 9.45%, respectively. Motion amplitude was strongly correlated with dose deviations (r>0.7). In contrast, 4D robust plans significantly improved dose stability, with discrepancies in D min and D 98 between 3D and 4D dose metrics reduced to within 1.4%. Robust optimization led to a significant decrease in the conformity index (CI) in 3D scenarios, but the CI of these robust plans significantly improved in 4D evaluations (P<0.01). Furthermore, under 4D evaluation, robust plans maintained clinically acceptable target conformity, with no statistically significant differences observed compared to conventional plans in most configurations. OAR doses remained within clinically acceptable limits for both conventional and robust plans. Conclusions Liver LRT is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, resulting in notable target dose deterioration under conventional planning. Four-dimensional robust optimization demonstrated the ability to address motion-induced uncertainties and facilitate robust target coverage while maintaining favorable conformity in 4D scenarios through necessary high-dose volume expansion. These findings highlight the importance of integrating motion-aware optimization and patient-specific motion management strategies in clinical LRT planning.

title: Automated quantitative computed tomography grading of lumbar facet joint degeneration: influence of segmentation errors on instance-level clinical assessment.
abstract: Background Automated lumbar facet joint degeneration grading requires both accurate anatomical segmentation and clinically meaningful region-level classification. We evaluated whether voxel-level segmentation performance was aligned with downstream degeneration grading. Methods This retrospective study included 145 lumbar computed tomography (CT) examinations and 725 level-specific bilateral facet joint regions of interest (ROIs), including 165 severe and 560 non-severe regions. Weishaupt grades 0-1 were categorized as non-severe and grades 2-3 as severe. Scheme A used binary nnU-Net segmentation followed by 11 quantitative region-level features, training-fold-specific standardization, and logistic regression; an oracle comparison using ground-truth masks was compared with analysis using predicted masks. Scheme B used direct three-class segmentation. Patient-level five-fold cross-validation was performed, with 116 training and 29 validation patients per fold. The results were reported as mean ± standard deviation (SD). Results Scheme A achieved a binary segmentation Dice coefficient of 0.770±0.008. In the oracle comparison, the region-level area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), recall, F1-score, accuracy, and case-level accuracy were 0.671±0.100, 0.538±0.172, 0.399±0.102, 0.640±0.051, and 0.579±0.096, respectively. Using predicted masks, the corresponding values were 0.650±0.068, 0.603±0.250, 0.375±0.072, 0.563±0.123, and 0.545±0.071. Scheme B achieved a native nnU-Net mean validation Dice of 0.493±0.044 and region-level AUC, recall, F1-score, accuracy, and case-level accuracy of 0.730±0.024, 0.445±0.051, 0.510±0.045, 0.808±0.015, and 0.738±0.058, respectively. Conclusions Voxel-level segmentation and clinically oriented grading performance were not directly aligned. Scheme A provided stable anatomical segmentation but more variable downstream grading, whereas scheme B achieved better overall region- and case-level classification performance but lower severe-degeneration recall. Both spatial and clinical decision metrics should therefore be considered when evaluating automated facet joint grading systems.

title: Ultrasonic texture features for assessing abnormal interventricular septum motion following cardiac surgery.
abstract: Background Cardiac surgery alters cardiomyocyte geometry and architecture, leading to changes in the acoustic properties of the myocardium. This study investigated ultrasomics-a novel cardiac ultrasound-based radiomics technique that extracts high-throughput pixel-level information from images-to identify ultrasonic texture and morphological changes associated with abnormal motion of the interventricular septum (IVS) following cardiac surgery. Methods A total of 650 patients from two centers were included in the study. The 460 patients from Center A were randomly allocated to the training (n=322) and internal validation (n=138) sets at a 7:3 ratio, while the 190 patients from Center B constituted the independent external validation set. All patients underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at two time points: 10 minutes after anesthesia induction (preoperative) and 10 minutes after chest closure (postoperative). Standard left ventricular long-axis and four-chamber views were acquired to visualize the IVS. The workflow consisted of IVS segmentation, radiomics feature extraction, and feature selection using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) algorithm. Three machine learning methods were compared: logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM). Model interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Results Twenty-six significant radiomics features, including shape, first-order, and texture features, were identified. The incidence of postoperative abnormal IVS motion was 50.93%, 46.38%, and 40.00% in the training, internal validation and external validation sets, respectively, with no significant intergroup difference (P>0.05). The SVM model demonstrated the best diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.943 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.925-0.961] in the training set, 0.948 (95% CI: 0.921-0.974) in the internal validation set, and 0.803 (95% CI: 0.772-0.834) in the external validation set. Postoperative analysis revealed significant changes in the core IVS radiomics features. Specifically, increased gray-scale heterogeneity and decreased texture correlation in the IVS were observed in patients with abnormal septal motion after cardiac surgery (all relevant P<0.001). Conclusions This study demonstrates the potential of cardiac ultrasomics to differentiate between normal and abnormal IVS motion in patients after cardiac surgery. A highly interpretable SVM ultrasomics model was developed based on texture and morphological features, providing quantitative characterization of microstructural changes in the IVS associated with abnormal motion following cardiac surgery and potentially supporting more precise perioperative clinical decision-making.

title: Development of a nomogram integrating contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging radiomics and clinical parameters for differentiating brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma from cerebral tuberculomas.
abstract: Background Cerebral tuberculomas and brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma are often indistinguishable on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), leading to misdiagnosis. This study develops a contrast-enhanced MRI radiomics-based nomogram to accurately differentiate them. Methods A total of 482 patients (290 males, 192 females; mean age 56.08±12.96 years), including 254 with cerebral tuberculomas and 228 with brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma were enrolled from two centers. Radiomic features were extracted, standardized, and reduced via significance testing, Pearson correlation, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. A radiomic model was built, then integrated with clinical predictors into a nomogram. Performance was assessed across training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results A total of 13 radiomic features were selected for model development. The radiomic model demonstrated areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.907, 0.891 and 0.886 in training, internal validation, and independent external validation cohorts, respectively, significantly outperforming models based solely on clinical factors, which achieved AUCs of 0.781, 0.712, and 0.828 (P<0.05). The nomogram, which integrated the radiomic scores (Rad-scores), age, ring enhancement, meningeal thickening, and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels, exhibited superior performance with AUCs of 0.951, 0.937, and 0.940 across the three cohorts. DCA demonstrated that the nomogram provided greater clinical net benefits across a range of threshold probabilities, and calibration curves indicated strong consistency between predicted probabilities and actual outcomes. Conclusions A nomogram combining clinical factors and contrast-enhanced MRI radiomics accurately differentiates cerebral tuberculomas from brain metastases of bronchial carcinoma, offering robust decision support for individualized diagnosis and treatment.

title: Native T1 mapping radiomics for assessing FIB-4-associated fibrosis risk in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
abstract: Background The fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) is widely used for noninvasive fibrosis risk stratification in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but it does not directly characterize spatial heterogeneity within the hepatic parenchyma. This study aimed to investigate whether native T1 mapping radiomics features are associated with continuous FIB-4 values in patients with MASLD, after accounting for hepatic steatosis and iron deposition with the goal of enabling early identification of liver fibrosis. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 124 patients with MASLD who underwent multiparametric liver magnetic resonance imaging, including proton density fat fraction (PDFF), iron (R 2 *), and native T1 mapping. To prevent data leakage, a 5-fold cross-validation framework was employed for radiomics analysis; variance thresholding, univariate Spearman correlation, and elastic net regression with nested cross-validation were performed sequentially within each training fold for feature selection and Z-score standardization. FIB-4 was treated as a continuous biochemical index, and two hierarchical regression models were refitted on the full dataset to evaluate the incremental value of the selected native T1 radiomics features beyond baseline liver fat (PDFF) and iron (R 2 *) content (Model 1: baseline; Model 2: baseline + radiomics features). In addition, we conducted an age-adjusted sensitivity analysis by including age as an additional covariate in both models to examine whether the contribution of radiomics features persists after accounting for age-related imaging variability. Results Twelve robust radiomics features were retained through the cross-validation selection pipeline. Model 1 showed limited explanatory ability for FIB-4 values (R 2 =0.028, adjusted R 2 =0.012, P=0.179). After incorporating the selected native T1 radiomics features, Model 2 demonstrated a significantly improved model fit (R 2 =0.455, adjusted R 2 =0.376; ΔR 2 =0.427; F-change =6.004, P<0.001). Root mean square error decreased from 0.167 to 0.133, and mean absolute error decreased from 0.132 to 0.106. In the age-adjusted sensitivity analysis, after controlling for age, PDFF, and R 2 *, the inclusion of radiomics features still significantly increased the explained variance, raising R 2 from 0.428 to 0.631 (ΔR 2 =0.203, P<0.001). Conclusions Using FIB-4 as a clinical reference, and after excluding the effects of PDFF and R 2 *, a significant within-sample correlation was observed between the radiomics features generated by native T1 mapping and FIB-4 values, indicating its potential clinical utility in the noninvasive assessment of fibrosis-related biochemical risk trends in patients with MASLD.

In the age-adjusted sensitivity analysis, after controlling for age, PDFF, and R2*, the inclusion of radiomics features still significantly increased the explained variance, raising R2 from 0.428 to 0.631 (ΔR2=0.203, P<0.001).

Conclusions

Using FIB-4 as a clinical reference, and after excluding the effects of PDFF and R2*, a significant within-sample correlation was observed between the radiomics features generated by native T1 mapping and FIB-4 values, indicating its potential clinical utility in the noninvasive assessment of fibrosis-related biochemical risk trends in patients with MASLD.

title: Development and validation of a deep learning model integrating 18 F-FDG PET/CT radiomics and clinical features to predict major pathological response in non-small cell lung cancer patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy.
abstract: Background Pathological complete response (pCR) and major pathological response (MPR) are early measures of treatment efficacy with prognostic relevance in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Individual biomarkers such as programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and tumor mutational burden (TMB), and conventional imaging interpretation, incompletely characterize treatment sensitivity. Integrating clinical biomarkers with radiomics may improve prediction by combining information on host factors and tumor biology with quantitative imaging measures of tumor heterogeneity. We aimed to develop and validate a model predicting pathological response. Methods We retrospectively collected fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) images and clinical data from 320 patients with NSCLC at Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital who received at least two cycles of chemoimmunotherapy followed by surgical resection and had postoperative pathological response assessments. Patients were randomly assigned to training (n=256) and validation (n=64) cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. A total of 1,834 CT and 179 PET radiomics features were extracted and integrated with demographic and tumor metabolic parameters, PD-L1 expression, TMB, and peripheral blood biomarkers. Following standardization and within-modality Pearson correlation filtering, features were selected using recursive feature elimination (RFE). A modality-aware attention model was developed to generate patient-specific scores for predicting MPR, including pCR. The model's performance was further validated in an external cohort of 31 patients from two independent hospitals. Results A total of 351 patients were included: 256 in the training cohort (160 responders and 96 non-responders), 64 in the internal testing cohort (35 responders and 29 non-responders), and 31 in the preliminary external test cohort. Our study proposes a modality-aware attention model, which was constructed upon RFE feature engineering technique. Our model integrates diverse data sources, including nine clinical characteristics, nine CT features, and nine PET features. Our model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.7467 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.6826 to 0.8159] in the training set. In the external independent validation cohort, the AUC was 0.7017 (95% CI: 0.5126 to 0.8715), with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 86%. Compared to single-modality models based on clinical features (AUC =0.6931; 95% CI: 0.6232 to 0.7604), the modality-aware attention model significantly improved accuracy. Conclusions The multimodal model showed potential for predicting MPR, including pCR, in patients with NSCLC receiving chemoimmunotherapy. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed before clinical implementation.

title: PET/CT radiomics for noninvasive histologic risk stratification in resected lung adenocarcinoma: a single-system development and internal validation study.
abstract: Background Preoperative histologic characterisation of lung adenocarcinoma is typically available only after resection. We evaluated whether fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) radiomics could predict histologic patterns and pathologic risk features using a hierarchical modelling strategy. Methods This retrospective cohort study included patients from three imaging facilities within a single academic health system. Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative PET/CT and CT segmentations; preprocessing included feature filtering, standardisation, redundancy reduction, and ComBat harmonisation. Penalised generalised linear model (GLMNET), random forest, and XGBoost models were trained with stratified cross-validation and evaluated in independent test sets. Outcomes included mucinous phenotype, non-mucinous histologic subtype, histologic grade, spread through air spaces (STAS), vascular invasion, and visceral pleural invasion (VPI). Eligible patients had primary lung adenocarcinoma treated by curative-intent resection, with preoperative PET/CT or thin-section CT and histopathologic review available; patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy, non-adenocarcinoma histology, or rare adenocarcinoma variants were excluded. The histologic reference standard was central review by a single thoracic pathologist per the 2021 WHO/IASLC (World Health Organization/International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer) classification, blinded to imaging and radiomic results. From 300 candidate radiomic variables (147 PET-derived, 153 CT-derived), models were developed using a 75%/25% stratified train-test split within the same single-institution cohort; the test set therefore represents internal, not external, validation. Results Among 254 patients, 255 tumours were analysed. Binary identification of poorly differentiated tumours (grade 3 vs. grade 1-2) achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) 0.767 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.624-0.897], area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) 0.854 (95% CI: 0.723-0.952), and satisfactory calibration [Brier Score 0.170; Brier Skill Score (BSS) 0.23]. VPI yielded a moderate global signal (ROC-AUC 0.691, 95% CI: 0.518-0.841). Non-mucinous subtype classification showed preserved probabilistic ranking despite limited categorical accuracy (balanced accuracy 0.614). Models for mucinous phenotype, STAS, and vascular invasion showed limited discrimination; VPI in the small-tumour subgroup was constrained by insufficient positive events. Conclusions PET/CT radiomics supported probabilistic preoperative risk stratification of lung adenocarcinoma, particularly for identifying poorly differentiated tumours. These results support radiomics as a complementary preoperative tool pending external validation.

title: Adult Cervical Deformity: Contemporary Evaluation, Classification, and Surgical Decision-Making.
abstract: ➢ Standing full-spine radiographs are mandatory for cervical deformity evaluation; key alignment targets include cervical sagittal vertical axis (cSVA) of ≤40 mm, T1 slope minus cervical lordosis (T1S - CL) of <15°, and a chin-brow vertical angle (CBVA) between -10° and +10° relative to the true vertical. The achievement of these thresholds is independently associated with better patient-reported outcomes, whereas values outside these ranges are associated with worse disability and quality-of-life scores.➢ The Kim-International Spine Study Group (ISSG) morphology-based classification, which identifies 4 patterns (flat neck, focal, cervicothoracic, and coronal or complex) from standing and dynamic extension radiographs, provides a reproducible morphology and flexibility-based framework that informs operative planning and has demonstrated superior interrater and intrarater reliability over prior descriptive systems; final surgical decisions integrate flexibility, neurological status, global alignment, bone quality, and patient-specific factors, and the direct impact of this classification on surgical outcomes requires further prospective validation.➢ Surgical planning is stratified by the intended lower instrumented vertebra (LIV) (Type 1: LIV T2-T4; Type 2: within the cervical spine or cervicothoracic junction; Type 3: extending past the thoracolumbar junction) and by whether the deformity is ankylosed, which determines the need for osteotomy.➢ Overall complication rates exceed 50% in prospective multicenter data; systematic risk mitigation, including neuromonitoring, tranexamic acid, staged approaches, and frailty-based patient selection, is essential for safe outcomes.➢ Despite high complication rates, the surgical correction of cervical deformity yields clinically meaningful improvements in pain and health-related quality of life at 1 year in appropriately selected patients; realistic goal-setting and individualized alignment targets are the keys to durable success.

title: Temporal Macrophage Activation Is Reduced by CCR2 Knockout in a Murine Subacromial Impingement Model.
abstract: Background Rotator cuff (RC) tendinopathy is a prevalent cause of shoulder pain and disability, yet its underlying molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Increasing evidence highlights the role of early inflammation and macrophage activation in symptom development and disease progression. C-C chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2) regulates monocyte recruitment and pro-inflammatory macrophage signaling in tendinopathy. This study characterizes the temporal inflammatory profile of RC tendinopathy and evaluates the impact of CCR2 knockout in a murine subacromial impingement (SAI) model. Methods Sixty mice (40 C57BL/6J wild type [WT SAI] and 20 CCR2 knockout [CCR2KO]) underwent bilateral placement of a subacromial surgical clip to induce RC impingement. Four additional C57BL/6J mice underwent sham surgery (WT sham controls). Animals were assessed through 42 days. Macrophage activation was quantified using microPET/CT (micro-positron emission tomography/computed tomography) and gallium-68-labeled folate receptor ligand. Selected WT SAI mice were killed at early and intermediate time points for temporal gene expression profiling. The remaining mice were killed on day 42 for histological, biomechanical, or gene expression analyses. Results WT SAI mice demonstrated a reproducible pattern of early macrophage activation, peaking on postoperative days 3 and 7. CCR2KO mice exhibited significantly reduced macrophage activation at these time points. Gene expression analysis of WT SAI supraspinatus tendons revealed early upregulation of inflammatory and M1 macrophage-related genes, followed by later increases in anti-inflammatory mediators and M2 macrophage-related markers. CCR2KO tendons demonstrated fewer tendinopathic changes on histology but did not exhibit superior biomechanical properties compared with WT SAI tendons. Conclusions RC tendinopathy exhibits a distinct early inflammatory phase characterized by macrophage activation and M1 macrophage-dominant signaling. CCR2KO reduces early inflammatory activity and may attenuate tendon degeneration. Clinical relevance Defining the inflammatory progression of RC disease may help to refine treatment strategies-particularly the use and timing of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, corticosteroid injections, and emerging biologic therapies. CCR2 represents a potential therapeutic target for modulating early inflammation and improving tendon healing.

title: Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty for Symptomatic Charcot Arthropathy.
abstract: Charcot arthropathy of the hip and knee is a progressive neuropathy-driven joint destruction process that is frequently misdiagnosed and often presents with discordance between symptoms and radiographic severity, requiring a high index of suspicion. Initial management centers on nonoperative strategies-including off-loading, immobilization, and pharmacologic modulation of bone turnover-to halt disease progression rather than restore function. Total joint arthroplasty (total knee arthroplasty and total hip arthroplasty) can substantially improve pain and function in patients with symptomatic Charcot arthropathy who fail conservative treatment, despite limited high-level evidence. Arthroplasty in Charcot joints is technically demanding and associated with significantly higher complication rates (approximately 20%-30% for total knee arthroplasty and up to 45%-58% for total hip arthroplasty), with instability, infection, and mechanical failure among the most common complications. Successful outcomes depend on careful patient selection, optimization of modifiable risk factors (e.g., glycemic control), and appropriate implant selection (e.g., constrained or dual mobility constructs), underscoring the importance of meticulous preoperative planning and multidisciplinary care.

title: Core Muscle Injury: A Combined Orthopaedic and General Surgery Algorithmic Approach for Diagnosis, Imaging, and Treatment.
abstract: » Core muscle injury (CMI) is a common cause of groin pain in athletes and reflects pathology of the inguinal canal, rectus abdominis-adductor longus (RA-AL) aponeurosis, and pubic symphysis. » There is a substantial lack of consensus on terminology and diagnostic criteria for CMI, hindering standardized evaluation, management, and research initiatives. » Diagnosis relies on structured history, physical examinations, and provocative maneuvers to identify CMI and concurrent pathology, and fluid-sensitive pelvic magnetic resonance imaging to characterize RA-AL injury. » Treatment strategies differ across sports medicine physicians, general surgeons, and orthopaedic surgeons, underscoring the need for early cross-departmental referrals to ensure all contributing pathologies are comprehensively identified and addressed. » When both adductor/RA-AL aponeurosis and inguinal canal/abdominal wall pathologies are present, prioritizing collaborative cases between orthopaedic and general surgeons is essential for decreasing operating room time, streamlining rehabilitation, and optimizing return-to-sport outcomes.

title: Proximal Scaphoid Pole Reconstruction Utilizing Ipsilateral Proximal Hamate Autograft.
abstract: Background Proximal pole scaphoid fractures complicated by nonunion and osteonecrosis present a challenging scenario with few good reconstructive options, especially when the proximal fragment is small or fragmented 1-4 . The use of an ipsilateral proximal hamate osteochondral autograft has emerged as a promising technique for reconstructing the proximal scaphoid pole, with the potential to restore carpal mechanics while avoiding the morbidity associated with free vascularized bone grafts or distant autograft sites. Description The procedure involves replacing the diseased proximal scaphoid with a structurally matched osteochondral graft from the ipsilateral proximal hamate. After excising the necrotic or fragmented scaphoid pole, a size-matched graft-harvested with its attached volar capitohamate ligament-is rotated 180° on its longitudinal axis to replicate normal scaphoid anatomy. The defect is measured in 3 planes using the scapholunate joint (proximal) and viable distal scaphoid surface as boundaries. On the hamate, an osteotomy is marked 8 to 10 mm distal to its proximal tip, parallel to the articular surface. The volar capitohamate ligament is preserved to guide graft orientation and maintain stability. These measurements align with recent anatomic and biomechanical studies that have confirmed 6 to 10-mm grafts accurately reproduce scaphoid morphology without compromising carpal kinematics. The graft is then inserted into the defect and secured with rigid internal fixation (headless compression screws or Kirschner wires). Residual gaps may be filled with cancellous bone graft. Scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) reconstruction is typically performed by suturing the hamate's volar capitohamate ligament to the dorsal SLIL remnant on the lunate with a 2-0 nonabsorbable suture. In patients with a partially intact SLIL, such as after failed fixation, the hamate graft alone may provide adequate stability, making formal reconstruction unnecessary. If intraoperative findings reveal dorsal scapholunate instability or an attenuated SLIL, reconstruction is indicated. Healthy, tensionable ligament remnants are repaired directly or reinforced with suture anchors. When dorsal fibers are deficient but volar remnants remain, the attached volar capitohamate ligament is used for reinforcement. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient begins a structured hand therapy program. Alternatives Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts (e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis 1,2 . These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal restoration of wrist biomechanics. Rationale The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting to salvage procedures. Expected outcomes Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the level of the contralateral wrist. Complications are rare but include nonunion, donor-site pain, and persistent stiffness. Important tips Limit proximal hamate resection to approximately 10 mm distal to its tip in order to replicate the scaphoid defect size while maintaining carpal stability.Ensure preservation of the triquetrohamate and volar capitohamate ligaments, as their integrity prevents instability.Rotate the graft 180° on its longitudinal axis in order to correctly orient the articular surfaces.Fixation should be rigid but not violate adjacent cartilage.Supplement with a distal radial bone graft if a distal scaphoid defect is present.Early controlled motion prevents stiffness. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient begins a structured hand therapy program.

Alternatives

Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts (e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis1,2. These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal restoration of wrist biomechanics.

Rationale

The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting to salvage procedures.

Expected outcomes

Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the level of the contralateral wrist. Complications are rare but include nonunion, donor-site pain, and persistent stiffness.

Important tips

Limit proximal hamate resection to approximately 10 mm distal to its tip in order to replicate the scaphoid defect size while maintaining carpal stability.Ensure preservation of the triquetrohamate and volar capitohamate ligaments, as their integrity prevents instability.Rotate the graft 180° on its longitudinal axis in order to correctly orient the articular surfaces.Fixation should be rigid but not violate adjacent cartilage.Supplement with a distal radial bone graft if a distal scaphoid defect is present.Early controlled motion prevents stiffness.

title: All-Suture Fixation for Acute Turf Toe Injuries.
abstract: Background Turf toe is a hallux metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) injury caused by hyperextension of the great toe with axial loading 1,2 . High-grade injuries may threaten return to sport and require surgery 3,4 . Here, we describe a capsular reconstruction of the great toe MTPJ with all-knotless suture anchors and suture tape augmentation for turf toe injuries, in isolation or in combination with a traumatic bunion, designed to reduce suture burden, minimize soft-tissue irritation, and facilitate recovery. Description The procedure begins with the patient supine. A direct medial approach to the hallux MTPJ is performed. Both the medial base of the proximal phalanx and the medial eminence of the metatarsal head are drilled at isometric points, and augmentation with suture tape is then performed. Isometric drill holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for suture tape augmentation. A knotless suture anchor is placed approximately 3 mm proximal to the articular margin of the metatarsal head, repairing the medial capsule in a horizontal mattress fashion. An additional knotless anchor is placed at the plantar plate insertion, and the suture is passed through the tibial sesamoid sling and tensioned with the toe in 20° of plantar flexion. Suture tape is secured into the proximal phalanx with an interference screw, then passed through the deep capsule into the metatarsal head, followed by the placement of an additional interference screw into the metatarsal head. The anchor is inserted into the plantar-medial proximal phalanx at the flexor hallucis brevis insertion. The toe is flexed during tensioning, then adjusted per clinical examination and the sesamoid location beneath the metatarsal head. Knotless fixation permits incremental tensioning with intraoperative assessment of motion. Final tensioning is performed with the toe in neutral to correct deformity without overconstraint, preserving range of motion. Alternatives Nonoperative alternatives include rest, ice, compression and elevation; anti-inflammatory drugs; activity modification; and brief immobilization 5,6 . Operative alternatives include primary capsuloligamentous complex repair with nonabsorbable sutures, plantar plate advancement with bone tunnels or suture anchors if primary repair is not feasible, and concomitant procedures such as sesamoidectomy and bunionectomy based on the injury pattern 2,7,8 . Rationale This technique is intended for high-grade turf toe injuries with capsuloligamentous disruption, sesamoid complex insufficiency, and MTPJ instability. Nonoperative treatment may be appropriate in cases of low-grade injury; however, persistent pain, instability, or loss of push-off strength following nonoperative treatment would indicate a higher-grade injury. Compared with isolated repair or plantar plate advancement alone, this technique restores both static and dynamic stabilizers of the hallux MTPJ while addressing associated angular deformity. Suture tape augmentation resists recurrent hyperextension and valgus forces while allowing controlled physiologic motion. Knotless, low-profile suture anchors minimize bulk and hardware prominence in a region with limited soft-tissue coverage and bone stock. This construct offers a robust reconstruction option for athletes requiring predictable restoration of stability and reliable return to sport. Expected outcomes Operative treatment of high-grade turf toe injuries has been shown to result in reliable pain relief, restored stability, and high rates of return to sport 8 . Previous studies have suggested improved function and earlier return to play compared with prolonged nonoperative treatment in appropriate patients 6,7 . Knotless suture anchors reduce implant prominence and eliminate knot-related irritation, while the small insertional diameter of the suture anchors preserves bone stock in the metatarsal head and proximal phalanx. This construct provides immediate stability while allowing controlled motion, facilitating rehabilitation, and reducing postoperative stiffness. Athletes typically return to unrestricted activity within 6 to 9 months, aided by the suture tape augmentation allowing earlier movement through the range of motion. This augmentation reduces the need for long-term spica splinting and bracing and reduces the risk of recurrence. Important tips The small anchor diameter and use of suture tape allow easy access without hardware burden.○ Suture choice depends on surgeon preference regarding construct stiffness and on the tissue quality and risk of irritation. We believe that suture tape lays flatter and, if required, knots are smaller.Avoid suture twisting or kinking, which can prematurely lock anchors, compromising fixation.○ After the anchor is placed, we keep the suture tape secured out of the field as we prepare the capsule with absorbable suture. As we load the second anchor, we maintain tension on the tape to prevent twisting.Overtightening the MTPJ capsule may lead to altered biomechanics. title: Co-occurrence of spinocerebellar ataxia type 16 and IDH-mutant oligodendroglioma associated with compound heterozygous STUB1 variants: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia type 16 (SCAR16), caused by biallelic STUB1 variants, is a rare cerebellar degenerative disorder. While STUB1 (encoding CHIP) is increasingly recognized as a tumor suppressor in gliomas, the co-occurrence of SCAR16 and intracranial glioma has not been systematically reported. This study aims to characterize the clinical, radiological, and genetic features of this unique comorbidity and explore the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Case presentation: We report a 35-year-old woman with a 7-year history of progressive gait ataxia. Initial cranial MRI revealed diffuse cerebellar atrophy. Whole-exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous STUB1 variants: a nonsense mutation (c.352C>T, p.Gln118Ter) and a missense mutation (c.433A>C, p.Lys145Gln), confirmed by familial segregation analysis. At age 33, serial MRI detected a new right temporal lobe lesion. Surgical resection was performed, and histopathology confirmed a WHO grade 2 IDH-mutant oligodendroglioma. Postoperatively, the patient received adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. Conclusions: This case provides the first clinical evidence linking biallelic STUB1 loss-of-function to both neurodegeneration and gliomagenesis. We propose a dual-pathway model wherein STUB1 deficiency impairs neuronal protein quality control (leading to cerebellar atrophy) and relieves tumor-suppressor restraint in glial cells (increasing susceptibility to IDH-mutant glioma). These findings expand the phenotypic spectrum of STUB1-related disorders and underscore the necessity of genetic screening in adult-onset ataxia with atypical features.

title: Deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognostic prediction in locally advanced cervical cancer through 18 F-FDG PET/CT and MRI combination
abstract: Abstract Background Precise pretreatment risk stratification is critical for guiding treatment intensification and personalized follow‑up in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). This study developed and validated a deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognosis prediction in patients with LACC treated with CCRT, using dual-modal pretreatment imaging from 18 F-FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI. Methods We retrospectively collected 346 patients (276 for training and 70 for testing) with LACC between June 2016 and October 2021. Radiomics and deep learning signatures were extracted from PET/CT and MRI. These signatures were integrated with the clinicopathological factors into a nomogram for clinical applications. Models were constructed using eleven machine learning algorithms, and a clinical-radiomics-deep learning model (CRDLM) was developed. The evaluation of the model’s performance was conducted through the metrics of the area under the curve (AUC). Results The CRDLM demonstrated superior predictive performance (AUCs of 0.998 (95% CI: 1.00–1.00) for training cohort and 0.901 (95% CI: 0.83–0.97) for testing cohort), which is significantly superior to conventional clinical factors (FIGO stage and SCC-Ag, AUC = 0.605–0.658). In addition, the CRDLM which combined radiomics with deep learning significantly outperformed the radiomics‑only model (AUC = 0.793, p = 0.006). Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of CRDLM reached 0.947, 0.725, and 0.786, respectively. Conclusions The CRDLM provides robust prediction of disease progression in LACC patients who received CCRT, which may facilitate personalized treatment strategies and improve clinical outcomes. Further validation in multicenter prospective studies is warranted.

title: MESO-FAP: Protocol for a Phase 1a/1b Study of [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 Radioligand Therapy Combined with Nivolumab and Ipilimumab in Advanced Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma
abstract: Abstract Background Malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) remains an aggressive malignancy associated with poor prognosis despite advances in systemic therapy. Dual immune checkpoint blockade with nivolumab and ipilimumab has improved survival outcomes and is established as a first-line treatment option for unresectable disease; however, durable responses occur in only a subset of patients, and treatment resistance remains common. Increasing evidence implicates the tumour microenvironment, particularly cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and stromal-mediated immune exclusion, as important contributors to therapeutic resistance. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), highly expressed on activated CAFs within mesothelioma stroma, represents a promising theranostic target. FAP-directed radioligand therapy using [ 177 Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 has demonstrated favourable tumour targeting and encouraging preclinical anti-tumour activity and may enhance anti-tumour immunity through modulation of the tumour microenvironment. Results MESO-FAP is an investigator-initiated multicentre phase 1a/1b study evaluating [ 177 Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab in patients with unresectable or advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma. The study comprises a dose-escalation phase using a conventional 3 + 3 design followed by a dose-expansion cohort. Eligible participants must demonstrate FAP-positive disease on screening [ 68 Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET/CT. Primary endpoints include safety, dose-limiting toxicities, determination of the maximum tolerated dose, and establishment of the recommended phase 2 dose. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include treatment response, survival outcomes, radiation dosimetry, molecular imaging biomarkers, and integrated translational analyses incorporating tissue and blood-based biomarkers. Conclusions MESO-FAP is the first prospective study investigating FAP-targeted radioligand therapy combined with dual immune checkpoint blockade in mesothelioma. The study incorporates a theranostic framework integrating molecular imaging, dosimetry, and translational biomarker analyses to establish the safety profile and recommended Phase 2 dose of stromal-directed radio-immunotherapy in MPM while generating mechanistic insights to guide future biomarker-driven clinical development. Trial registration Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR), ACTRN12626000505303. Registered 23 April 2026, https://anzctr.org.au/Trial/Registration/TrialReview.aspx?id=391496&isReview=true

title: Towards UASC-Net: A Pilot Study of Uncertainty-Aware 3D Brain Tumor Segmentation on BraTS 2021
abstract: Abstract Brain tumor segmentation from multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a central component of treatment planning and disease monitoring, but reliable voxel-wise annotation is costly and difficult to obtain. This work presents a pilot evaluation of UASC-Net Lite v2, an uncertainty-aware extension of a compact 3D U-Net baseline for binary tumor segmentation from multimodal BraTS 2021 MRI patches. The model combines a 3D encoder–decoder segmentation pathway with attention-, prototype-, and uncertainty-related auxiliary outputs, enabling spatial confidence inspection alongside mask prediction. Experiments were conducted on a reproducible 16-case pilot subset (13 training and 3 validation cases), using 64×64×64 patches and eight training epochs. After validation-set threshold calibration, the proposed model achieved a pooled Dice score of 0.7381 and IoU of 0.5849, compared with 0.7297 and 0.5744 for the TinyUNet3D baseline. UASC-Net Lite v2 improved sensitivity from 0.7681 to 0.8609, while specificity and precision changed from 0.9685 and 0.6949 to 0.9532 and 0.6460, respectively. Qualitative visualizations show the segmentation outputs together with uncertainty and attention maps. These results should be interpreted as a pilot study rather than a full benchmark: threshold calibration was performed on the validation patches and the cohort is small. Nevertheless, the experiment provides reproducible evidence that uncertainty-aware modeling can improve lesion recall and overlap under limited-data conditions.

title: Poorly Differentiated Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Regaud–Schmincke Type of the Posterior Pharyngeal Wall: Diagnostic Challenges and Pitfalls
abstract: Abstract Background: Oropharyngeal tumors may initially present with nonspecific inflammatory symptoms, leading to diagnostic delay. Large exophytic lesions of the posterior pharyngeal wall are uncommon and may clinically and radiologically mimic infectious or inflammatory conditions. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 67-year-old male presenting with progressive dysphagia, intermittent dysphonia, and foreign body sensation in the throat. Initial clinical evaluation and histopathological examination suggested an inflammatory process. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a large polypoid mass arising from the posterior pharyngeal wall, extending to the left salpingopharyngeal fold and the hypopharynx, with craniocaudal extension of approximately 64 mm and significant airway narrowing. Repeat biopsy followed by surgical excision confirmed poorly differentiated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma of the Regaud–Schmincke type with deep soft-tissue infiltration, including invasion of striated muscle and salivary gland parenchyma. Due to impending airway obstruction, protective tracheostomy was performed prior to surgery. The postoperative course was complicated by transient acute kidney injury, which resolved with conservative management. The patient subsequently completed adjuvant external beam radiotherapy and was successfully decannulated four months postoperatively. Follow-up imaging demonstrated no evidence of local recurrence or distant metastasis. Conclusion: This case highlights the diagnostic challenges posed by exophytic oropharyngeal carcinomas presenting with inflammatory features and underscores the importance of cross-sectional imaging and repeat histopathological evaluation in patients with persistent or progressive pharyngeal symptoms.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Maternal Serum sFlt-1, PlGF, and the sFlt- 1/PlGF Ratio in Placenta Accreta Spectrum and Their Correlation With Placental Immunohistochemical Expression
abstract: Abstract Background Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is associated with substantial maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly because of severe obstetric haemorrhage. Although antenatal imaging remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, additional biomarkers may have potential value, particularly where access to advanced imaging is limited. This study evaluated maternal serum soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1), placental growth factor (PlGF), and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio in women with PAS and examined their relationship with placental immunohistochemical expression. Methods This prospective case–control study was conducted at Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi, in collaboration with the ICMR–National Institute of Pathology. Women with singleton pregnancies beyond 28 weeks with confirmed or clinically diagnosed PAS were enrolled as cases, while age- and gravidity-matched women undergoing caesarean delivery without PAS served as controls. Maternal plasma sFlt-1 and PlGF concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Placental tissue was evaluated by histopathology and immunohistochemistry for sFlt-1 and PlGF. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to account for baseline clinical differences. Results Sixty women were included in the final analysis, comprising 40 PAS cases and 20 controls. Median plasma sFlt-1 concentrations were lower in PAS cases than controls (23.5 vs. 29.8 ng/mL; p = 0.034), whereas PlGF concentrations were higher (270.5 vs. 48.2 pg/mL; p = 0.006). The median sFlt-1/PlGF ratio was significantly lower in PAS cases (88.1 vs. 561.1; p = 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.670 for sFlt-1, 0.716 for PlGF, and 0.753 for the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio. At the selected cut-offs, sFlt-1 showed 100% sensitivity and 65% specificity, PlGF showed 62.5% sensitivity and 100% specificity, and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio showed 62.5% sensitivity and 95% specificity. None of the three biomarkers differed significantly according to histopathological depth of invasion. In multivariable logistic regression, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio was not independently associated with PAS after adjustment for maternal age, parity, previous caesarean delivery, and previous placenta previa ( p = 0.110). Placental PlGF immunohistochemical expression showed a significant positive association with plasma PlGF concentration ( p < 0.001), whereas sFlt-1 tissue expression was uniformly weak. Conclusions Maternal plasma sFlt-1, PlGF, and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio were significantly different in women with PAS compared with controls and demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance. title: Can Chest CT Differentiate Between Low-Risk and Higher Risk Congenital Lung Lesions in Infants?
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether chest CT can differentiate low-risk congenital lung lesions (pulmonary sequestration and CPAM type 2) from higher-risk lesions (CPAM type 1 and pleuropulmonary blastoma [PPB]) and thereby support the selection of patients for conservative management. Methods In this retrospective study (2003–2024), we identified infants with congenital lung lesions who underwent chest CT and subsequent pathologic confirmation. Two pediatric radiologists independently reviewed the anonymized CT scans, blinded to clinical and pathologic data. Lesions with a systemic arterial supply or predominant hyperinflation were classified as low risk; those with a solitary cyst, a cyst > 2 cm, or a complex cyst without systemic supply were classified as higher risk. Diagnostic confidence was graded as low, moderate, or high. Pathologic diagnosis served as the reference standard, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess interobserver agreement. Results Eighty-three children (52 male) were included. Low-risk lesions (n = 73) comprised CPAM type 2 with or without sequestration (n = 51), isolated sequestration (n = 18), and other benign lesions (n = 4). Higher-risk lesions (n = 10) included CPAM type 1 (n = 8) and type I PPB (n = 2). For moderate-to-high-confidence diagnoses, sensitivity was 100% for both radiologists; specificity was 89.2% and 93.1%; and the negative predictive value was 100%. Interobserver agreement was almost perfect (98.4%; κ = 0.95). Conclusion Chest CT enables reliable differentiation of higher-risk from low-risk congenital lung lesions and can guide the selection of candidates for conservative management.

title: Auditable Federated Learning for Multimodal Brain Tumor Classification under Label Skew and Client Dropout
abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) allows hospitals to collaboratively train deep learning models without exchanging patient images, but reported FL studies in medical imaging often assume independent and identically distributed (IID) client data and full participation in every communication round both conditions seldom hold in real clinical networks. Furthermore, although the entire premise of FL rests on the iterative averaging of client weight updates, the optimisation dynamics of those weights are rarely audited at the round level, limiting clinicians' and regulators' ability to inspect how the global model evolves under stress. This study presents an auditable federated framework for binary brain-tumour classification from a combined multimodal dataset of 4618 axial computed-tomography (CT) and 5000 magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI) slices, totalling 9618 labelled images. A lightweight three-block convolutional neural network is trained across five simulated clients using FedProx with proximal coefficient µ = 0.01 and FedAvg aggregation, under two contrasting client partitions: an IID scenario in which each client receives a balanced sample of healthy and tumour cases, and a deliberately aggressive non-IID scenario in which each client is assigned an 80% majority class. Clinically realistic stress is added by dropping a randomly chosen client in approximately 30% of rounds. At every round, for every active client, the framework records three weight summaries initial (received from the server), updated (after local training), and aggregated (new global model) together with per-client accuracy, loss, precision, recall, F1-score, communication payload, wall-clock round time, and process memory. After ten communication rounds, the global model attains 96.05% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.9641 on the held-out test set under the IID partition, and 94.96% accuracy with F1 0.9547 under the 80% label-skew non-IID partition, corresponding to an IID-to-non-IID degradation of only 1.09 percentage points despite the severe class skew and 30% per-round client dropout. Inspection of the weight-audit trace reveals a consistent and measurable shift in the output-layer mean under non-IID training that is invisible in conventional accuracy curves, suggesting that round-level weight auditing can serve as a lightweight forensic signal of distributional drift in federated medical AI.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics and Machine Learning for Predicting Refractory Outcomes in Ménière’s Disease: A Multicenter Preliminary Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the value of a machine learning model based on radiomics features derived from multicenter gadolinium-enhanced inner ear magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting refractory clinical outcomes in patients with Ménière’s disease (MD). Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients with unilateral Ménière’s disease diagnosed at two medical centers between January 2019 and December 2023. A total of 154 patients from Center 1 constituted the internal dataset and were divided into a training set (n = 123) and an internal test set (n = 31) at an 8:2 ratio, while 32 patients from Center 2 were included as an independent external validation set. According to established clinical guidelines, patients were categorized into good-control and poor-control groups. Radiomics features were extracted from the cochlea and vestibule on gadolinium-enhanced 3D-FLAIR-CUBE images, and bilateral difference (Diff) features were generated by subtracting contralateral ear features from those of the affected ear. Feature selection was performed using correlation filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Multiple machine learning algorithms were used to construct predictive models, which were evaluated in both internal and external datasets. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score, and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis (DCA). Results In both the training and internal test sets, the Diff radiomics model achieved higher AUCs than the symptomatic-ear radiomics models (training set: 0.815 vs. 0.682; internal test set: 0.730 vs. 0.650), along with improved sensitivity and F1 scores. Feature importance analysis indicated that vestibular-related radiomics features contributed more prominently to the prediction of refractory outcomes. Although model performance declined in the external validation set, the Diff model maintained high sensitivity (0.957) and F1 score. DCA demonstrated greater clinical net benefit of the Diff model in the training and internal test sets. Conclusion A machine learning model based on bilateral difference radiomics features can effectively predict refractory outcomes in MD and demonstrates superior performance compared with single-ear radiomics models. This approach may provide objective imaging support for prognostic assessment and individualized management of patients with MD.

title: Unintentional Weight Loss Preceding Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report and Review of Possible Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Background Unintentional weight loss is not a recognized presenting feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is more commonly associated with malignancy, chronic infection, endocrine disorders, gastrointestinal disease, or systemic inflammatory conditions. We report an unusual case in which marked involuntary weight loss preceded the diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Case Presentation: A 37-year-old man presented with acute gait impairment and right lower-extremity weakness. Retrospective history revealed gradual unintentional weight loss from approximately 97 kg to 68 kg over nearly two years despite preserved appetite and the absence of gastrointestinal, infectious, endocrine, or constitutional symptoms. Extensive investigations, including laboratory testing, infectious screening, tumor markers, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasonography, and chest imaging, failed to identify an alternative cause. Neurological examination demonstrated right lower-extremity weakness, generalized hyperreflexia, bilateral pyramidal signs, and an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 4.0. Brain and cervical spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple typical demyelinating lesions fulfilling the 2017 McDonald criteria for MS. The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by rituximab (1000 mg every 6 months). During four years of follow-up, the EDSS score improved from 4.0 to 1.0, MRI studies remained stable, and body weight gradually returned to two years before the start of the disease. Conclusion This case describes marked, unexplained weight loss preceding the diagnosis of RRMS, which resolved after treatment initiation and disease stabilization. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association suggests that clinically significant weight loss may represent an uncommon and underrecognized manifestation of active MS. Further studies are needed to clarify the frequency and mechanisms of weight changes in MS.

title: Transcutaneous Skin Perforation by a Protruding Xiphoid Process in a Bedbound Patient With Post-Traumatic Cervical Myelopathy: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background The xiphoid process is the smallest and most morphologically variable component of the sternum, and anterior (ventral) deviation is a recognized anatomical variant. Symptomatic xiphoid disease typically presents as localized pain (xiphodynia). Cutaneous complications are exceedingly uncommon, and only a single previous report describing an ischemic xiphisternal ulcer associated with a protruding xiphoid has been published. To the best of our knowledge, we identified no previous English-language report describing complete transcutaneous perforation of the skin by a protruding xiphoid process associated with chronic sinus formation and secondary infection. Case presentation A 71-year-old bedbound man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and post-traumatic cervical myelopathy with spastic weakness developed progressive protrusion of the xiphoid process. The angulated xiphoid tip gradually eroded through the overlying skin, producing a chronic midline ulcer with sinus tract formation and superimposed infection. Lateral radiography demonstrated marked anterior angulation of the xiphoid process with prominent ventral protrusion and irregularity of the distal tip. The patient underwent xiphoidectomy with en-bloc excision of the ulcer and debridement of devitalized soft tissue. Intraoperative culture of the resected xiphoid specimen yielded extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli, and culture-directed carbapenem therapy was administered. Histopathological examination revealed extensive ulceration with inflamed granulation tissue and a sinus tract, accompanied by reactive squamous epithelial hyperplasia (pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia), whereas the underlying bone was unremarkable and showed no evidence of malignancy. Conclusions A protruding xiphoid process can rarely progress beyond pain and superficial ulceration to cutaneous breach with sinus tract formation and secondary infection, particularly in debilitated patients with chronic immobility, diabetes mellitus, and reduced soft-tissue padding. This process appears mechanistically analogous to a pressure ulcer developing over an atypical bony prominence. Xiphoidectomy combined with debridement and culture-directed antimicrobial therapy appears to provide definitive treatment. Histopathological examination is essential because reactive pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia at the ulcer margin may mimic cutaneous malignancy.

title: Enhancing Structural Quality in Medical X-ray Super-Resolution via Domain-Aware Loss
abstract: Abstract Upscaling medical X-ray images is more challenging than enhancing natural images, because preserving accurate structural and boundary information is more important for diagnostic correctness than producing a realistic appearance. Super-resolution methods such as SRGAN, ESRGAN, and the Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT) perform well on natural images, but when applied to medical images they can cause texture hallucination, obscure anatomical boundaries, and remove clinically important features. This study presents a comprehensive comparison of four approaches: standard SRGAN, standard ESRGAN with VGG-based perceptual loss, HAT with L1 loss, and the proposed optimised models ESRGAN_USELoss and HAT_USELoss, which incorporate a domain-specific loss function designed for X-ray imaging. The proposed USELoss (U-Net, Sobel and Edge Loss) replaces the computationally heavy VGG19 perceptual loss with a lightweight U-Net encoder that preserves multi-scale anatomical structures, and adds a Sobel-based edge loss to improve boundary accuracy, prioritising diagnostic fidelity over perceptual sharpness. On the PadChest X-ray dataset the quantitative results show large gains: standard ESRGAN reaches only 22.21 dB PSNR, whereas ESRGAN_USELoss reaches 34.04 dB, while HAT_USELoss achieves the best SSIM (0.9215) and LPIPS (0.1607). The proposed methods improve edge-preservation metrics by 5.5%, demonstrating that domain-specific loss functions are effective for clinically reliable medical image super-resolution. https://github.com/1aryantyagi/Segmentation-Paper is the Github repository of the code.

title: Double filtration plasmapheresis in anti-amphiphysin antibody syndrome mimicking multiple system atrophy: A case report
abstract: Abstract We retrospectively analyzed a patient with a positive anti-amphiphysin antibody status to characterize the clinical manifestations, diagnostic workup, and treatment results of anti-amphiphysin antibody disease that mimics multiple system atrophy (MSA), and we reviewed the relevant literature. The patient primarily presented with Parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia, and autonomic dysfunction. An 82-year-old male presented with a subacute onset of bradykinesia, ataxia, and severe orthostatic hypotension. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed hippocampal and cerebellar atrophy. Serum autoimmune neurological antibody testing was positive for anti-amphiphysin IgG (titer 1:320). Based on the multisystem involvement and exclusionary diagnostic workup, the patient was diagnosed with anti-amphiphysin antibody-associated MSA-like autoimmune neurological syndrome. After three sessions of double filtration plasmapheresis (DFPP) and sequential therapy with mycophenolate mofetil, the patient's motor function and orthostatic hypotension improved significantly. At the 6-month follow-up, the antibody titer decreased to 1:32, and the clinical condition remained stable. Anti-amphiphysin antibody syndrome can mimic MSA. Prompt neuronal autoantibody and long-term tumor screening are required for rapidly progressive atypical MSA-spectrum patients with severe autonomic failure. DFPP combined with immunosuppression achieves a favorable neurological prognosis.

title: Cephalothoracoomphalopagus Tetrabrachius Tetrapus Conjoined Twins: An Extremely Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Conjoined twins are a rare subset of monozygotic twins that usually have a poor prognosis, which has become a significant cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality. This case highlights the importance of routine antenatal care for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins. Case presentation: A 31-year-old G2P1 female in 29 4/7 weeks of gestation was referred from a primary health care center to our hospital with conjoined twins. Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) ultrasonography examinations at 29 4/7 weeks of gestation revealed one fetal head accompanied by an orbital hypotelorism with an interocular diameter of 0.99 cm. The liver and heart were found to be the fusion organs involved. Polyhydramnios was observed with a maximum vertical pocket of 12.07 cm. Diagnosis of cephalo-thoraco-omphalopagus conjoined twins was made right after the first scan and consistently confirmed thereafter by six more repeated ultrasound examinations. Clinical examination after scheduled surgical delivery in 33 5/7 weeks old neonates revealed male conjoined twins with a fused head accompanied by two pairs of ears, along with a single trunk together with four neurologically independent upper limbs and lower limbs, as well as two complements of genitalia and two anuses. The twin showed signs of respiratory distress and died within one hour of birth. Conclusion Routine antenatal care and advanced ultrasound scanning are crucial for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins.

title: A novel sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) in treating intrabony defects of stage III periodontitis – Case Series
abstract: Abstract Background Sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) is a minimally invasive approach in which graft material is introduced into the intrabony defect through a pinhole made on the facial surface opposite to the intrabony defect alveolar crest and apical to the junctional epithelium 4 weeks following minimally invasive non-surgical therapy. This strategy is intended to keep the long junctional epithelium as a biologic seal over the grafted material, while providing maximum soft tissue support around the grafted material. Methods This case series presents the short-term outcome of ten patients diagnosed with stage III grade A periodontitis with interproximal intrabony defects of at least 3 mm, treated with S-PHT. Xenogenic graft material was introduced into the defect through a facial pinhole opposite to the alveolar crest following defect degranulation using minimally invasive hand and ultrasonic instrumentation. Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded at baseline (4 weeks after non-surgical therapy) and at 9 months following S-PHT. Results Nine months following S-PHT, all sites measured ≤ 4mm probing pocket depth (PPD). The number of sites with clinical attachment level (CAL) gain ≥ 3mm was 6 out of the 10 reported cases. Six sites out of the 10 cases fulfilled a composite outcome of pocket closure of ≤ 4 mm with ≥ 3 mm attachment gain and no bleeding on probing. Significant improvement in intrabony defect fill reported after 9 months with a mean defect fill of 3.1 mm (< 0.001). Conclusions This case series demonstrates that S-PHT, as a minimally invasive approach, could be a reliable patient friendly option for treating intrabony defects in stage III periodontitis. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov. identifiers NCT07763223 PRT-RCT-2026-001 (05-08-2026 and retrospectively registered 19-08-2026)

title: A Decade-Old Retained Intrapleural Glass Fragment in an Asymptomatic Skydiver: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Retained intrathoracic foreign bodies are usually discovered after a traumatic event that the patient clearly remembers. Glass, however, can be especially problematic. It is frequently retained, may be missed during the initial assessment, can appear variably on imaging, and may migrate months or even years after injury rather than becoming securely encapsulated. To our knowledge, an entirely asymptomatic intrapleural glass fragment discovered incidentally in a skydiver has not previously been reported. We describe a 34-year-old male skydiver who was referred after a routine screening chest radiograph showed an abnormal shadow in the right hemithorax. Ten years earlier, he had sustained a penetrating right-sided chest injury during a parachute landing, when he crashed through a window. At that time, he was treated for haemopneumothorax with intercostal drainage, but no foreign body was suspected or actively sought. On current examination, he had a contracted right hemithorax. Computed tomography revealed a radio-dense pleural foreign body. Right-sided thoracotomy was performed, and a 7 × 2.5 cm glass fragment was removed from dense pleural adhesions. His postoperative recovery was uneventful, and he later returned to skydiving.
